text:
ATLANTA -- Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was able to leave an area hospital, return to the locker room and rejoin his teammates after what appeared to be a serious-looking injury led to him getting carted off the field during Atlanta's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears on Sunday.

With the Bears leading 21-7 with 8:48 left in the third quarter, Daniels dived in to tackle Colston Loveland after a Caleb Williams pass completion, and the linebacker's head appeared to collide with the tight end's left leg near the knee.

Daniels remained down on the field for some time as medical personnel tended to him. They stabilized his neck and body, then loaded him onto the cart in a gurney as Falcons players and coaches gathered around and wished him well.

The team said Daniels had movement in all of his extremities and was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. Daniels then surprisingly was able to come back to Mercedes-Benz Stadium and was walking in the locker room under his own power after the game.

On the way off the field during the third quarter, Daniels made a fist with his left hand.

"He said, 'Y'all go finish this off,'" quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. "He was in good spirits."

Added coach Kevin Stefanski: "Those are no fun for anybody. Players, coaches. You don't want to see anyone down like that. Kendal is a kid we all love, we all respect."

Daniels is a 23-year-old rookie linebacker.

He's an impressive athlete, measuring 6-foot-5 and 242 pounds.

He split his college career between Oklahoma State and Oklahoma.

Daniels was chosen by the Falcons in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft at the No. 134 overall pick.

Entering Sunday, he had played in five games in his rookie season. He had 22 tackles, including 2.0 tackles for loss. He has 1.0 sack and one pass defensed so far this season.

text:
ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams put his right hand underneath his ear as he skipped off the field at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, a motion to encourage the raucous crowd of Chicago Bears fans on hand to get even louder.

Williams let out a guttural "Let's go!" and threw his right fist in the air following the Bears' 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The quarterback then made his way through the tunnel toward the visitors locker room where he posed a question to a handful of media members waiting to speak with him after he received one of two game balls in his return from a hamstring injury that had sidelined him the past three weeks.

"Y'all like that?" Williams said, smiling.

Williams didn't miss a beat in his return for the Bears (4-2) on Sunday, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown and showing no physical limitations from the injury he suffered Sept. 20.

"I felt confident from the jump," Williams said of his return. "When I get out there, I'm going to feel confident in my leg, in myself and in my guys and the O-line. So I just let it rip, let these guys go make plays for us, get first downs and score touchdowns."

Williams said his body felt "great" postgame despite four sacks. With the Bears playing the New England Patriots on Thursday, Williams will prioritize treatment amid a quick turnaround.

"Felt great to get hit after three weeks of just rehabbing," he said. "So [I] feel strong, feel good. Obviously got to go and take care of it this week. It's going to be a weekly thing, just taking care of it, staying up to date on it and taking care of my body."

Chicago jumped out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter after Williams led the offense on back-to-back touchdown drives. He completed his first 12 passes, the most at any point in a game in his career.

"Honestly, I didn't even know that he hadn't missed yet," coach Ben Johnson said. "That's not even something -- it's more you just kind of calling it. You're doing what you feel like is going to help your guys out. But when I reflect back, it's not a surprise. I know we had a couple big plays there on third-and-long that were really the key part of keeping those drives going there early in the game.

"The fact that we started fast, really in all three phases, was huge for us, as well as something that we had also talked about the night before. Just if you could write a script, that's what we would want to do against a team like this. We've got to come out of the gate hot, and it's a dangerous team. Their defense is darn good. Their offense can put up points in a hurry, as we saw at the end of the game. And I thought the way that our guys came out and responded was huge. Having Caleb back was a huge part of it."

The Bears went 9-of-17 on third down, which allowed the offense to extend drives and stay on the field for 40:08. After entering Week 6 with the league's worst red zone scoring efficiency (42.86%), the Bears were 4-for-4 Sunday, excluding Williams' kneel-down at the end of the game.

Ahead of the Bears' trip to Atlanta, Williams completed his first week of practice with full participation since suffering what he classified as a "pretty serious" hamstring tear late in a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Midway through the week, Williams had a one-on-one meeting with Johnson in which he voiced a desire to open up the passing attack upon his return.

"I walked in his office, dapped him up and said, 'Let's get this thing going this week,'" Williams said. "I walked out after that."

That approach paid off quickly Sunday.

"He was connecting everywhere," wide receiver Rome Odunze said. "People were making plays all over the field. So our offense was really clicking. That's why we want to be in that flow state mode, and we were in there today."

In the process of recording his sixth career 300-yard passing game, which broke a tie with Mitchell Trubisky for the most such games by a Bears player before turning 25 years old, Williams set a career-high completion percentage (83%). He also completed all 26 of his attempts when Atlanta failed to generate pressure, which marked the most attempts without an incompletion since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009.

Days after Williams expressed frustration over how his hamstring injury was reported and the negative reaction he received on social media for his emotions after getting injured, his teammates rallied in support of the quarterback and the energy his return provided.

title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return with knee injury after attempting tackle on kickoff return
description:
The Los Angeles Rams' special teams woes continued with a very odd situation Sunday, with kicker Blake Grupe being ruled out of the game with a knee injury after attempting a tackle.
That left punter Ethan Evans as the only option for the Rams at kicker, with the 25-year-old attempting — and making — his first extra point in his NFL career.
With no other kicker on the roster, Evans filled in if the Rams need to attempt a field goal or extra point.

Los Angeles waived Mevis after he missed two field goals (one was blocked) in last week's three-point loss to the Buffalo Bills.
text:
The Los Angeles Rams' special teams woes continued with a very odd situation Sunday, with kicker Blake Grupe being ruled out of the game with a knee injury after attempting a tackle. That left punter Ethan Evans as the only option for the Rams at kicker, with the 25-year-old attempting — and making — his first extra point in his NFL career.

Just days after he signed with the team as a free agent, Grupe started against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, scoring a field goal in the first quarter. But on the kickoff, Grupe broke up a 40-yard return from Devin Duvernay by knocking the Cardinals receiver out of bounds — and Grupe paid for it.

Grupe went into the locker room before he was eventually ruled doubtful. He was later downgraded to out.

With no other kicker on the roster, Evans filled in if the Rams need to attempt a field goal or extra point.

With the shaky kicker situation, the Rams tried to avoid kicking when possible. After scoring a touchdown in the second quarter, the team went for a 2-point conversion. Matthew Stafford was sacked and fumbled on the attempt, with the Cardinals recovering.

Other plays indicated a reluctance to use Evans. Late in the first half, the Rams got the ball at their own 35-yard-line with 46 seconds remaining, but opted to let the clock run out instead of get closer to the end zone. In the fourth quarter, Los Angeles went for it on fouth-and-8 at the Arizona 44, out of field-goal range; the Rams failed to convert.

As the Rams tied things up with a touchdown with a minute remaining, they had to rely on Evans for the go-ahead extra point. Evans, who had placekicking duties in college and high school, had never attempted an extra point in the NFL — but he nailed it.

The Cardinals, however, beat the Rams 18-16 after hitting a walk-off field goal. The loss puts Los Angeles at a stunning 2-4 record.

Grupe was signed by the Rams earlier last week as a free agent, replacing Harrison Mevis as the starting kicker. Los Angeles waived Mevis after he missed two field goals (one was blocked) in last week's three-point loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Evans has spent his entire NFL career with the Rams, getting selected in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft.

title: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy misses halftime after 'freak' on-field injury - USA Today
description:
Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy coached the second half of his team's NFL Week 6 game against Tampa Bay with a foot injury.
The 62-year-old told reporters after his team's 26-19 victory that his foot was stepped on leading up to halftime.
"Mike McCarthy, heading off the field, and appears to have twisted his ankle," CBS play-by-play announcer Andrew Catalon observed as the broadcast returned from studio coverage at the half.
What happened to Mike McCarthy?
CBS sideline reporter AJ Ross called the injury a "freak thing" as McCarthy was walking to speak with her at halftime.
text:
Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy coached the second half of his team's NFL Week 6 game against Tampa Bay with a foot injury.

The 62-year-old told reporters after his team's 26-19 victory that his foot was stepped on leading up to halftime. The CBS broadcast reported that the 62-year-old spent halftime in the blue medical tent on the Steelers' sideline instead of joining his team in the locker room. He was seen limping on the field at Raymond James Stadium, favoring his right foot.

"Mike McCarthy, heading off the field, and appears to have twisted his ankle," CBS play-by-play announcer Andrew Catalon observed as the broadcast returned from studio coverage at the half. "You can see him slow up, and then needing a little assistance.

"He went right into the blue medical tent, and he spent the entire halftime in the tent. He just came out. He never went to the locker room at halftime as he was getting his leg looked at."

What happened to Mike McCarthy?

CBS sideline reporter AJ Ross called the injury a "freak thing" as McCarthy was walking to speak with her at halftime. Cameras did not capture exactly what happened, but he told reporters that the discomfort was caused by being stepped on and not by rolling his ankle.

The veteran is in his first season as coach of his hometown team after 18 seasons with Green Bay and Dallas. He is the offense's play-caller, so any departure from the playing surface would have been a change to the team's process.

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers said afterward that the injury disrupted little about the team's routine, though there was concern among players.

"There wasn't a whole lot different at halftime," Rodgers said. "It was still the same chaos, but people said Mike didn't come in and people were wondering what the heck's going on. Is he OK? Glad he's OK."

Cameras showed McCarthy standing on the sideline throughout the second half, so the mishap did not appear to impact his ability to stay involved in the game. His offense rallied from a 13-3 halftime deficit to tie the game late in the fourth quarter, then win in overtime.

Kendal Daniels was carted off the field on Sunday on a back board.

Kendal Daniels Hospital Update

That's the public hospital for the city of Atlanta.

It's the 10th-largest public hospital in the United States and is a Level I trauma center.

Is Kendal Daniels Moving?

The Falcons update did share that Daniels was able to move all his extremeties.

Given the fact that he laid immobile on the turf, that's a crucial update.

Who is Kendal Daniels?

Daniels is a rookie linebacker and 23 years old. He's originally from the state of Oklahoma, where he was ranked No. 5 among the safety class in his senior year of high school.

He split his college career between Oklahoma State and Oklahoma. He was the Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year at OSU.

He's an impressive athlete, measuring 6-foot-5 and 242 pounds. He ran a 4.76-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine and vertical leaped 29.5 inches.

Daniels was chosen by the Falcons in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft at the No. 134 overall pick.

Entering Sunday, he had played in five games in his rookie season. He had 22 tackles, including 2.0 tackles for loss. He has 1.0 sack and one pass defensed so far this season.

Daniels was having the best game of his career on Sunday. He already had seven tackles, including one for a loss.

His playing time had increased because Divine Deablo had already exited the game with an arm injury and been ruled out.

Daniels attempted a low tackle on Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland.

Loveland's right knee hit Daniels directly in the facemask, though, essentially a smash right to the front of his head.

It left Daniels on the ground for quick attention from the trainers, and at least the first update from the Falcons is a good one relative to how the scene on the field looked.

text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- On the day the New England Patriots welcomed back receiver A.J. Brown, they lost their other top receiver, Romeo Doubs, to a shoulder injury.

Doubs left Sunday's 26-19 win over the New York Jets after diving to haul in a 42-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Drake Maye with 4:10 remaining in the first quarter. He was initially announced as questionable to return before the team ruled him out early in the third quarter.

Doubs landed hard on his shoulder on the play after reaching a top speed of 21.44 mph to track down Maye's heave, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, which was the fastest speed he has reached as the ball carrier in his five-year career. The Patriots signed him to a four-year, $68 million deal in March as one of their top free agent targets, then traded for Brown in June to give Maye a new 1-2 combination.

Brown hurt his ankle in Week 1, was placed on injured reserve and returned to game action Sunday.

In addition to Doubs, Patriots starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker injured his hamstring in the second quarter and was later ruled out.

Starting right tackle Morgan Moses also left the game in the second quarter due to an ankle injury. After initially being announced as questionable to return, he was downgraded to out at the start of the fourth quarter.

And guard/center Ben Brown was ruled out in the fourth quarter with a knee injury.

The Patriots (4-2) have a quick turnaround after Sunday's game, visiting the Chicago Bears on Thursday.

Coach Mike Vrabel said he didn't have definitive updates on any of the players, but cast doubt that they would be available for that game.

"We are all smart people here; it's a short week," Vrabel said. "Whether they can make it back or not, I don't know. They didn't finish [this] game and that's a quick turnaround."

There was no progress for Monangai in Week 6, at least in terms of his practice participation, as the former seventh-round pick did not practice at all before being ruled out.

After two absences in a row for Monangai, here's what we know about his return timeline moving forward.

Kyle Monangai's return timeline

As head coach Ben Johnson said again this past week, there is no plan to put Monangai on injured reserve, which would have forced him to sit out a minimum of four games.

That means the Bears don't expect Monangai to sit out more than three games, which on the surface puts him in play to return in Week 7 against the New England Patriots.

However, the Bears have to play on a short week, with the game versus the Patriots taking place on Thursday, so Monangai won't have as much time as he normally would to get right, and it looks like he's going to need every day he can get since he still hasn't practiced since his injury.

Knowing all that, it's safe to assume that Monangai is going to be back in Week 8 against the Seattle Seahawks, at the earliest, instead of Week 7.

With the short week, the Bears will release their first injury report on Monday, and that injury report will likely be an estimation.

That said, any semblance of estimated participation would be good news for Monangai's chances of suiting up.

Kyle Monangai injury update

Last week, head coach Ben Johnson provided a positive update on Monangai.

While Johnson said once again that Monanga is week-to-week, he also noted how the Bears running back should avoid injured reserve and he's progressing in his recovery.

"It wasn't something we felt required an IR stint. It remains a week-to-week situation, but as far as I know, he's continuing to trend in the right direction," Johnson told reporters.

While it remains to be seen if Monangai will be back for Week 7 — again, we're skeptical that will happen — Johnson's update shows Monangai is getting better and that leaves us optimistic he won't be out longer than Week 8.

description:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy wasn't able to address his team as usual at halftime on Sunday in their overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
On his way to his halftime interview at Raymond James Stadium, McCarthy apparently injured his ankle.
He eventually decided to head straight into the blue medical tent on the sideline, where he remained for all of halftime.
Despite the injury, McCarthy continued coaching the team in the second half normally.
But a win is a win, and McCarthy's halftime injury didn't appear to hinder him much in the end.
text:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy wasn't able to address his team as usual at halftime on Sunday in their overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

On his way to his halftime interview at Raymond James Stadium, McCarthy apparently injured his ankle.

Broadcast cameras did not appear to catch the injury on video. Instead, McCarthy was shown having trouble as he tried to walk off the field at halftime. He eventually decided to head straight into the blue medical tent on the sideline, where he remained for all of halftime. He never made it back to the locker room to address the Steelers, and re-joined the team at the start of the third quarter.

Despite the injury, McCarthy continued coaching the team in the second half normally. His ankle injury appeared to be minor after all.

And, despite falling into a 13-point hole in the fourth quarter, Aaron Rodgers led the Steelers storming back to force overtime. He eventually found Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown pass in the extra period, too. The score was the first of Bernard's career, and lifted the Steelers to a second straight win.

Rodgers went 33-of-49 passing for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the win, which moved the Steelers to 4-2 on the season. They are in a great spot in the AFC North race, but the win in Tampa was much more complicated than it needed to be. Rodgers could have sealed the win in regulation, but couldn't find the end zone from the 3-yard line after Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels threw his second interception of the fourth quarter.

But a win is a win, and McCarthy's halftime injury didn't appear to hinder him much in the end. He and the Steelers can head home happy.

text:
OCTOBER 18: The news on Henderson is better than expected. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network reports the second-year RB is expected to play against the Jets in Week 6. Ditto left tackle Will Campbell, whose MCL sprain was expected to force him to miss time. With Brown also set to return, the Pats are getting closer to full strength.

OCTOBER 17: The Patriots are getting wide receiver A.J. Brown back from injured reserve in Week 6, but another of their notable offensive weapons could miss time. Running back TreVeyon Henderson has a high ankle sprain that is expected to shelve him for multiple games, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN.

Henderson will not require surgery, per Schefter, and an IR stint may not be necessary in this case. Although Henderson confirmed the sprain to Mike Reiss of ESPN and other reporters on Friday, he managed to practice on a limited basis this week.

The Patriots list Henderson as questionable on their injury report, leaving open the possibility that he could play against the AFC East rival Jets on Sunday. If Henderson can’t go, the Patriots will elevate Lan Larison from the practice squad to join Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as their backfield options, Reiss relays.

While splitting time with Stevenson in 2025, Henderson impressed during a 17-game rookie season. The second-round pick from Ohio State ran for 911 yards on 180 carries (good for a robust 5.1 average per attempt) and scored nine touchdowns. He also found the end zone once as a pass catcher and finished with 35 receptions for 221 yards on 42 targets. This season has not gone as smoothly for Henderson, who missed a Week 1 loss to the Seahawks with a different ankle injury and has rushed for just 163 yards on 42 attempts (3.9 YPC) in four games. He also hasn’t been as big of a factor through the air, having caught two of four targets for 22 yards.

On the other side of the ball, the 3-2 Patriots have had to make do without starting edge defender Harold Landry all season. Landry led the team in sacks (8.5) during its AFC title-winning campaign in 2025, but he began battling knee problems midway through the year. Those issues have continued into 2026, which forced the Patriots to place Landry on reserve/PUP at the end of August. While they still haven’t opened Landry’s 21-day practice window, head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that “the plan would be for him to return at some point” (via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald).

text:
Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for at least a month as he undergoes treatment for a superficial blood clot in his calf.

The Philadelphia Eagles placed their star quarterback on injured reserve Saturday afternoon, the team announced.

Hurts is set to miss at least the next four games, and on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers will be replaced by QB Tanner McKee as the Eagles' starting quarterback.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Philadelphia's decision to place Hurts on IR came after consultations with numerous doctors and experts about how to treat the signal-caller's blood clot.

The team first announced Hurts was dealing with a blood clot when they declared him out for Sunday's contest, and while doing so released a statement regarding the injury timeline.

Hurts sought medical treatment for his calf on Oct. 8 after he was cleated during Philadelphia's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, according to the statement. On Oct. 10, team medical staff performed an ultrasound following the Eagles' flight to London and a walkthrough session ahead of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The ultrasound revealed the blood clot, but doctors determined it was safe for Hurts to play.

He went 21 of 40 for 220 yards and a touchdown in another losing effort, but practiced back in the United States on Wednesday before undergoing a follow-up ultrasound that revealed movement in the blood clot.

The indication of movement set in motion the events this week, with the Eagles initially ruling Hurts out and gathering myriad medical opinions before opting to place him on IR.

Hurts heads to the sideline having lost three straight games to fall to 2-3. He's thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season with a 57.8 completion percentage that stands as a career low outside his rookie season.

His struggles are emblematic of an Eagles squad that has been in disarray due to injuries, performance and seemingly everything in between.

Wide receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert will be at McKee's disposal against Carolina, but they have each missed two games. Running back Saquon Barkley is set to miss his second contest due to a hamstring injury, and his primary backups, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, are on IR, leaving the Eagles to turn to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele in the backfield. Right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired on Oct. 6 after 13-plus seasons and six Pro Bowls, and Cam Jurgens, a Pro Bowler the past two seasons who endured a dreadful start to the '26 campaign, was traded to the Houston Texans a day later.

It's culminated in an offense that ranks 29th in points scored, which would match the franchise's worst finish since 2012. The Eagles haven't finished a season 30th in yards -- where they currently sit -- since 1999.

The onus to turn it around now shifts to McKee, who has thrown for 597 yards, five TDs and one INT in six career appearances with a 1-1 record as a starter. Behind him is Joe Milton III, signed off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Friday, and fifth-round rookie Cole Payton.

It's time for Nick Sirianni's crew to dig deep if they're to run the coach's streak of playoff berths to six since he took over the job.

In the meantime, Hurts will get the treatment he needs to ensure he returns to full health.

text:
Micah Parsons won't be on the field for a highly anticipated prime-time grudge match when his Green Bay Packers host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Oct. 18.

When might the three-time All-Pro edge rusher actually come make his comeback?

Ten months after he suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus in his left knee, Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list.

Yet while others were eager to see him square off against his former team with the "Sunday Night Football" spotlight firmly trained on him, the pass rusher said he wasn't going to expedite his recovery process just to make it back in time for the matchup.

"So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said last week on his podcast, "The Edge with Micah Parsons." "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it."

Micah Parsons injury update

Parsons has yet to be cleared to practice. Now set to sit out the Week 6 contest, the edge rusher will miss out on what he said over the summer would be the "most optimistic" timetable for a return.

In Parsons' mind, however, the wait for his season debut could end soon.

"If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl," Parsons said on his podcast. "But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first.

"What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL (tear) happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side."

Packers coach Matt LaFleur, who last week said he would play Parsons as soon as he was given "the green light," echoed that sentiment.

"(S)ometimes, you’ve got to make sure that your body is (in sync)," LaFleur said. "You don’t want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg is what I’m getting at.”

The Packers don't have their bye until Week 11, with a difficult stretch looming before the break. After the clash with the Cowboys, Green Bay faces the Detroit Lions on the road before hosting a "Thursday Night Football" showdown with the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers. A trip to take on the New England Patriots and a home game against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings then follow before the break.

How Packers defense is faring without Micah Parsons

Pressing on without Parsons has not been without its challenges for the Packers, who wilted down the stretch last season after their star defensive player was lost for the season in December.

Green Bay's most dramatic display on defense came in a Week 3 unraveling against the Atlanta Falcons on "Thursday Night Football." With quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returning to the lineup, Atlanta's previously dormant attack exploded for 498 yards in a 35-14 win. Running back Bijan Robinson rolled to 194 yards on the ground, while wide receiver Drake London added another 194 yards through the air.

From there, however, the Packers seemed to settle in with consecutive victories over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears, allowing a combined 21 points in the two contests.

Green Bay's pass rush has managed to generate a good deal of heat on opposing quarterbacks without Parsons in the fold, ranking fifth in pressure rate (42.5%), according to Next Gen Stats. Former first-round pick Lukas Van Ness, who largely struggled throughout his first three years as a pro, has stepped up to help fill the void by recording 21 pressures, the 10th-highest sum of any defender in the NFL so far this year.

But with all of their wins coming against offenses that have either been muted or shorthanded – the Bears were without quarterback Caleb Williams and running back Kyle Monangai in their loss – the Packers figure to be in for a sizable test in the coming weeks. Their next three opponents rank in the top eight for both scoring and EPA per play. The defense will also be without one of its other stars for the rest of the season after linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a season-ending torn Achilles in Week 4.

The New York Giants entered Sunday's Week 6 home game against the New Orleans Saints with encouraging injury news on two key players.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin) and linebacker Abdul Carter (calf) are both expected to play despite being listed as questionable. Thomas has managed his groin issue since Week 2 without missing a snap, while Carter's expected return provides a boost to a defense already without Brian Burns for the season.

Carter has recorded 2.0 sacks and ranks among the league leaders in quarterback pressures.

Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) was not addressed by Rapoport. Eluemunor, who suffered the injury in the Week 5 tie against Washington, practiced on a limited basis Friday after missing the prior two days and remains questionable.

Head coach John Harbaugh indicated Friday that both tackles were essentially full-go (but were listed as limited) and performed well, though Eluemunor's status appears less certain and could be a game-time decision. If he is inactive, second-year swing tackle Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle after filling in last week.

The Giants also ruled out cornerback Colton Hood (concussion), safety Tyler Nubin (neck) and tight end Theo Johnson (neck).

On the other side, Rapoport reported that Saints running back Alvin Kamara (back) and wide receiver Chris Olave (illness) are expected to play as well.

With Jameis Winston at quarterback in place of the injured Jaxson Dart, the Giants (3-1-1) will look to protect their lead in the NFC East against a 1-4 Saints team. Availability for Thomas and Carter strengthens their outlook, though the right side of the offensive line remains a variable heading into kickoff.

Two members of the New England Patriots are trending in a positive direction ahead of Sunday’s contest against the New York Jets, and are now considered “likely” to play in the game.

Starting left tackle Will Campbell and rotational running back TreVeyon Henderson both entered the weekend as questionable due to their respective knee and ankle injuries. However, after participating in practice throughout the week, the expectation is that they will be active against the Jets. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network was first to report the news.

Henderson, 23, went down in the second quarter of last week’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders and was unable to. return to the game. Initial reports indicated that he might miss “multiple weeks” with a high ankle sprain, but he was back on the practice fields already on Wednesday.

Campbell, 22, was hurt two plays after Henderson. He exited the game for the locker room and despite briefly returning to the sideline never reentered the contest. However, initial fears that he might “miss some time” because of a knee sprain did not turn out to be true; like his teammate, he also was back on the practice fields on Wednesday and available all three days.

Whether or not Henderson and Campbell will play a full workload against the Jets on Sunday will be seen. Last week, the team turned to third-string running back Corey Kiner and first-round rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu to replace them.

Regardless of their eventual participation level, Sunday’s report is the latest good injury news coming out of One Patriot Place. The team already activated wide receiver A.J. Brown off injured reserve on Saturday; he too is expected to play against the Jets.

Kickoff between the Patriots and their AFC East rivals at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

"Before you start asking, (I) do not know if I'm playing yet," the Chicago Bears quarterback told reporters Thursday while revealing he still must undergo stress testing and pass medical protocols before he will be cleared to return.

Williams suffered a hamstring injury during Chicago's Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. When he was carted off the field, Bears fans likely feared he would be lost for the season.

And while he seems to be ready to return, Williams said he wasn't happy with the reporting and reaction to his setback he called a "hamstring tear" that was "pretty serious."

Williams' status has been the biggest ongoing storyline surrounding the Bears.

He was listed as a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day on Thursday, suggesting he is nearing a return. What's more, he also changed his Instagram profile picture to a photo of John Wick with a bio that read, "I'm inevitable."

"He's doing a great job progressing and we'll see when we can make him available to help us win ball games," head coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday. "But he's itching to get back as soon as he can, which is a good thing, and when we get the green light, we'll move forward from there."

Johnson also said he believed the Bears "have three guys that can win games in this league."

Chicago has done more than just tread water during Williams' absence, as Case Keenum led it to a 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent directed a 23-12 win over the New York Jets.

However, things took a turn last Sunday in a 31-7 blowout loss to the rival Green Bay Packers.

Bagent started the game but played so poorly at 12-of-21 for 87 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions that Johnson put Keenum into the game to finish. It was a reminder the Bears likely need Williams healthy and under center quickly if they are going to have any realistic chance of repeating as NFC North champions.

Roman Wilson, who injured his hand in last week’s game against the Colts, was placed on IR on Saturday afternoon. He will miss at least the next four games and is eligible to return for the Nov. 22 game in Philadelphia at the earliest.

Wilson, who had already been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium, was off to the best start of his three-year career. He is third on the team in receptions (14) and receiving yards (188) and has two touchdown catches.

PHILADELPHIA -- The Carolina Panthers will have right tackle Taylor Moton (lung, blood clot) and defensive end Tershawn Wharton (neck) available for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.

The Panthers announced Saturday that Moton and Wharton had been activated from the non-football injury/illness and physically unable to perform lists, respectively. Running back Trevor Etienne (ankle) was also activated off injured reserve.

Carolina had three openings on its 53-man roster, so activating Moton, Wharton and Etienne was possible without corresponding moves. Moton and Wharton missed all of training camp and the preseason -- along with the first four games of the regular season -- with their ailments.

Moton had been listed as questionable to play after being a full participant in practice throughout the week. First-round pick Monroe Freeling has started in place of Moton throughout the first four games of his rookie season and offered mixed results. But Freeling sustained a knee injury in the Week 4 win over the Detroit Lions and was given a doubtful tag entering the weekend. Moton, now active, is likely to start at right tackle against the Eagles.

Wharton has been working his way back to the field since undergoing neck surgery in May. The veteran defensive lineman, who signed a three-year, $45 million deal last offseason, has been hindered by various injuries since arriving in Carolina in 2025. He has played just nine games for the franchise, producing 36 total tackles and two sacks.

Wharton, like Moton, was a full participant in practice and was listed as questionable on the final injury report. If active Sunday, he is likely to rotate with the likes of Bobby Brown III, second-round pick Lee Hunter and undrafted rookie Aaron Hall, opposite fellow starter Derrick Brown.

Etienne's return from injured reserve was signaled by coach Dave Canales last week. The coach confirmed that stance Friday. Etienne injured his ankle during the preseason finale against the Houston Texans in August and was subsequently placed on injured reserve ahead of the league's cut-down deadline. He was a full participant in workouts this week, and Canales said he was confident Etienne would play against Philadelphia following the final practice of Week 6.

With fellow running back AJ Dillon (ankle) ruled out for Sunday, Etienne, a 2025 fourth-round pick, could bring stability to the running back depth chart and the return game on special teams. Last season, Etienne had an up-and-down performance as the team's primary kick and punt returner, but Canales has said multiple times this season, even with Etienne on IR, that the former Georgia running back would be the primary option at both jobs upon his return.

Etienne is also likely to back up starting running back Chuba Hubbard in the backfield. The team also elevated running back Anthony Tyus III and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad to the game-day roster to provide additional support at their respective positions.

The Washington Commanders' final injury report lists a baker's dozen of players out or questionable, sure to create an availability problem for Washington facing the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Four players are officially listed as out: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin), Javontae Jean-Baptiste (pectoral), Marcus Mariota (knee), and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle). All four players missed practice all week. Nine additional players are also listed as questionable, including Stefon Diggs, Javon Kinlaw, and three safeties.

Of the three safeties, Percy Butler (hamstring) and Tyler Owens (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice but were upgraded to limited; Nick Cross (illness) was a full participant all three days but is still questionable. All three players missed last week's game against New York. Quan Martin improved from limited on Thursday to full participation on Friday and Saturday, with no game designation.

Stefon Diggs' return is possible; he's officially listed as questionable. He went from missing Thursday's practice to limited on both Friday and Saturday. Terry McLaurin has no game designation after being limited Thursday and Saturday and sitting out Friday with a hamstring/rest designation. Treylon Burks was also limited all three days but has no game designation. Getting Diggs back would give Jayden Daniels another option in the passing game after playing without him against the Giants.

The Commanders will also be without Croskey-Merritt in the backfield, but they should have options. Austin Ekeler was limited all week with a chest injury, while Rachaad White went from full participation Thursday to limited Friday and Saturday. Neither received a game designation. Jeremy McNichols was a full participant all three days but remains questionable with a quad injury. He would also need to be activated from injured reserve before he can play Monday.

Washington's defensive front is another area to watch with Omenihu and Jean-Baptiste both out. Kinlaw fully participated Thursday, missed Friday's practice, and returned Saturday on a limited basis. He's questionable with ankle and knee injuries. K'Lavon Chaisson, meanwhile, returned to full participation Saturday after sitting out Friday and has no game designation.

There are still a few roster decisions to make before Monday night. Trey Amos (ankle) and Jordan Magee (hamstring) are both questionable and, like McNichols, remain in their 21-day practice windows. Neither can play until they are activated from their respective reserve lists. Lucas Patrick is also questionable with an illness despite returning to full participation Saturday.

Washington knows which four players it won't have against San Francisco, but with nine more listed as questionable, the Commanders still have plenty to sort out before Monday night's kickoff.

text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The San Francisco 49ers will have to wait at least another week for the return of defensive end Nick Bosa, though there's at least a chance they'll have both receiver Mike Evans and fullback Kyle Juszczyk for Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders.

The Niners ruled Bosa out for Monday night as he continues to recover from a calf injury. Bosa had expressed optimism last week that he might be able to get back against the Commanders, and San Francisco held out some hope, too.

But Bosa didn't practice all week, and the 49ers made it official that his wait will continue Saturday afternoon.

"We would've been pleasantly surprised if he could go," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I was pleasantly surprised that he was that optimistic last week, but we still would've been surprised. So, this is kind of what we were expecting. There was a chance. He wasn't wrong when he said that. I think he felt that way, but we were going to make sure it was fully good and another week will help."

Evans, meanwhile, did not practice this week with what Shanahan called Achilles soreness coming out of last week's win against the Seattle Seahawks. He's listed as questionable for Monday night against Washington.

While Evans wasn't participating in practice, he did some conditioning on the side during each of the three practice viewing periods that reporters were able to watch.

Asked about Evans' status for the game, Shanahan said, "We'll know on Monday," though it's worth noting that Evans has already played in games this year after missing practices during the week with injury.

As for Juszczyk, he has no injury designation and will return from the knee sprain and bone bruise he suffered in Week 4 against the Denver Broncos. That injury was initially expected to keep Juszczyk out for two to three weeks, but he recovered quickly and was a full participant in practice Friday and Saturday after he was limited Thursday.

"It looked bad at the beginning, and they said they thought it would be three weeks," Shanahan said. "Juice has always been fast every time he's ever been hurt, but this was really impressive."

Elsewhere on the injury report, the 49ers ruled out receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring), safety Marques Sigle (ankle) and linebacker Garret Wallow (hamstring). Defensive tackle Gracen Halton (quadricep), safety Siran Neal (neck), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder), defensive lineman Mykel Williams and wideout Christian Kirk (calf) join Evans with questionable designations.

The 49ers opened Kirk's practice window this week after he'd been out since the beginning of training camp with a calf injury. He was a limited participant in all three days of practice with Shanahan saying Kirk could "possibly" play against the Commanders.

The blood clot that will keep Philadelphia Eagles star Jalen Hurts on the sideline for a Week 6 matchup against the Carolina Panthers is located in quarterback's calf and “superficial," according to the team.

Superficial blood clots in the leg differ from deep-vein thrombosis (DVT), but according to medical experts who specialize in blood clotting, should still be taken seriously.

“People often don’t think about it in athletes and people that don’t have a lot of the other risk factors, so I think getting the attention out there to symptoms that people should be evaluated with is important for both athletes and non-athletes alike,” Dr. Jordan Schaefer, a hematologist at the University of Michigan Health System and associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan Medical School, told USA TODAY Sports.

What is a superficial blood clot?

Superficial blood clots will often cause redness, pain or a cord-like lump that can be felt beneath the skin, according to Shcaefer. All blood clots carry the risk of breaking loose and moving toward the lungs, which could result in a pulmonary embolism, a potentially fatal event. Schaefer said superficial clots matter not only because of the symptoms, but also because 10 percent of patients experience the clot moving to the deep-vein system and becoming more serious.

It’s more common for clots to exist in the deep-vein system higher up the leg, Schaefer said. The Eagles said a follow-up ultrasound on Oct. 14 revealed movement in the small blood clot in Hurts' leg and ruled the Super Bowl 59 MVP out for Sunday’s game against Panthers.

Dr. Rushad Patell, who is a hematologist at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, Massachusetts, and is an associate professor of medicine at Harvard Medical School, wrote in an email to USA TODAY Sports that superficial vein thrombosis – or a blood clot – exists on a spectrum. Some cases are relatively low risk and require only symptomatic treatment, such as warm compresses, compression stockings and non-steroidal inflammatory drugs like Ibuprofen.

“Not all blood clots are preventable,” Patell wrote, “particularly when they occur following an injury.”

Jalen Hurts hurt during Rams' game

According to the Eagles’ statement, Hurts sought after treatment after his calf was stepped on during an Oct. 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. That type of trauma could potentially lead to a superficial blood clot. Trauma can damage the endothelium, which is the lining of the blood vessel, and can be injured – damage to the wall is one of the three classic mechanisms that contribute to blood clot formation, according to Patell.

“It is plausible that a cleat injury could have contributed to the development of a superficial clot,” Patell wrote. “However, without prior imaging, it would be impossible to establish whether the clot was already present or definitively attribute it to the injury.”

The Eagles said their medical staff deemed Hurts OK to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Oct. 11 in London, England, following an ultrasound the day before the game. The doctors said “mobility and activity were important,” according to the statement.

Schaefer thinks long periods of travel that could affect clotting for an athlete because of minimal blood flow – individuals aren’t moving much on a plane or bus.

Long-distance travel is a recognized, although relatively weak, risk factor for venous thrombosis, Patell wrote.

“It would be difficult to attribute any change in the clot to a single flight, particularly in the setting of a recent injury,” Patell wrote.

Repeat imaging can sometimes identify changes that lead clinicians to reconsider the initial management strategy for a clot and are necessary to track improvement. In a conservative approach, 72 hours would be considered a normal gap between exams, Schaefer said.

Superficial blood clot treatment options

There can be some variability in terms of the recovery depending on individual circumstances, Schaefer said.

“A lot of times, what we’re doing, is kind of following people closely over time,” Schaefer said. “It’s not like a one-time visit and then you’re done. It’s often reassessment in how you’re feeling and a physical of how the leg looks. Is that swelling and redness and exam getting better?”

Patell wrote that recovery depends on the location and extent of the clot and what type of treatment is required. The length of the clot is also a consideration, Schaefer said.

Patients with more extensive clots or those at higher risk for progression may require anticoagulation medication – blood thinners – for approximately 45 days.

If Hurts is being treated with blood thinners, Schaefer said, his recovery timeline would be more complicated because football is a contact sport. Blood-thinning medications increase the risk of serious bleeding with traumatic injuries, including internal bleeding.

Those are all obvious serious concerns. But the initial symptoms that brought Hurts into the Eagles’ training room – redness, leg pain, swelling, “things that don’t seem right,” Schaefer said – can be difficult to distinguish from a muscular injury.

“I think it’s important that people seek medical attention and work with their doctors to determine the appropriate treatment for their individual situation,” Schaefer said.

“Oftentimes, we want to catch these things kind of early,” Schaefer added. “It can get, potentially, worse.”

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles do not plan to place quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve at this time as they continue gathering information on the superficial blood clot in his calf, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Saturday.

Hurts, who was declared out on Oct. 15 for Sunday's game against the Panthers, is sidelined indefinitely, but a stint on IR would guarantee he misses at least four weeks.

Rapoport and Schefter added that there is still a chance Hurts ends up on injured reserve -- if he requires blood thinners, which he could not play football while using, the minimum timeframe for a moderate dose is typically six weeks. There is also a possibility that doctors could initially treat Hurts' clot with anti-inflammatories while monitoring the situation, per Rapoport and Schefter, who reported the best course of action and the ultimate decision on his return to play will come from Philadelphia's medical team.

The Eagles initially announced Hurts' injury on Thursday with a statement that provided a timeline of his superficial blood clot diagnosis.

According to the statement, Hurts had been cleated during Philadelphia's 24-20 Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Oct. 4, and on Oct. 8 sought treatment for his calf after practice. The team medical staff performed an ultrasound on Oct. 10 following the Eagles' flight to London and a walkthrough session for their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars, which revealed the blood clot. The doctors determined Hurts could safely play.

Hurts went 21 of 40 for 220 yards and a touchdown in the 19-17 loss and practiced in full on Wednesday, but that evening a follow-up ultrasound showed movement in the blood clot, leading the team to now hold him out and continue evaluating for the best course of action.

A three-time Pro Bowler, Hurts has struggled this season along with the rest of the 2-3 Eagles, throwing for 933 yards, eight touchdowns, three interceptions and completing just 57.8% of his passes while helming the 29th-ranked scoring offense.

He is now one of many Philly stars missing from the lineup. Although DeVonta Smith is set to face the Panthers after a two-game absence, Saquon Barkley will be sidelined for a second consecutive contest due to a hamstring injury. Barkley's backups, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, are both on inured reserve. Dallas Goedert is back but also missed two games, while the team's anchor at right tackle, Lane Johnson, retired on Oct. 6, and Philadelphia traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens a day later.

Quarterback Tanner McKee will replace Hurts to make his third career start Sunday as the Eagles continue to navigate some turbulent times. In six appearances, the 2023 sixth-round pick has gone 54 of 88 for 597 yards, five TDs and one INT. Philadelphia also signed Joe Milton III off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad and have rookie Cole Payton rostered, as well.

ATLANTA -- Chicago Bears nickel corner Kyler Gordon has been activated off the physically unable to perform list and onto the 53-man roster, the team announced Saturday.

Gordon spent the offseason rehabbing a calf injury that landed him on the PUP list at the start of training camp. He was moved to reserve/PUP on Aug. 30 and had to sit out the Bears' first four games.

He returned to practice Sept. 30 and has been a full participant in every session over the past three weeks.

"He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "I feel good about him -- whether that's this week or next week -- I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far."

In a corresponding move, the Bears placed defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo on injured reserve. Odeyingbo had already been ruled out for Week 6 with a quad injury sustained against the Green Bay Packers last week. Coach Ben Johnson said this week that Odeyingbo was expected to miss "some time" but that the Bears did not believe his injury was serious enough to warrant IR.

The Bears also released Xavier Woods, who started the last two games at safety, and signed defensive back Nick McCloud from the practice squad to the active roster.

Gordon was drafted 39th overall in 2022, the very first pick by Bears general manager Ryan Poles. Since then, the cornerback has totaled five interceptions, 17 passes defensed, 2.5 sacks, 10 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles.

Injuries were present during his first three seasons (2022-24) but did not stop the Bears from making him the NFL's highest-paid primary slot corner in April 2025 when he signed a three-year, $40 million extension with $31.25 million guaranteed.

Since signing his new deal, Gordon has struggled to stay on the field. He was limited to five games, including the playoffs, in 2025 due to multiple soft tissue injuries and spent two separate stints on injured reserve.

Last season, Gordon allowed 16 receptions on 24 targets for 243 yards and three touchdowns, according to Next Gen Stats. He allowed a passer rating of 139.4 in coverage, which was the third highest in the NFL among cornerbacks (minimum 20 targets), with only Trevon Diggs (154.6) and McCloud (142.2) allowing a higher passer rating.

After being sidelined for the Bears' offseason program and training camp, Gordon spent several weeks away from the team in September rehabbing on his own. He returned to Halas Hall ahead of Week 4 and made an impression on his coaches for how quickly he got up to speed on the practice field and in meetings.

"The one thing about Kyler, he's a sharp kid, or young man, I should say," Bears nickels coach Cannon Matthews said. "So that part I'm not worried about. Even just him being back in meetings, the questions that he asks has always been great that way. So honestly, there's still area for growth in that department, but I don't have any issue with him getting caught up to speed with the mental aspect."

The Bears could use some reinforcements in the secondary after Packers quarterback Jordan Love had six completions of 25-plus yards in Chicago's 31-7 loss.

Gordon has not played since the Bears-Rams divisional playoff matchup in January, so it is unrealistic to think he could play a full workload of 50 to 70 snaps, according to defensive coordinator Dennis Allen.

"I've said this before, I think that Kyler can help us win games," Allen said. "You know, when that time comes where he's able to be out there on the field and participate and help us win games, I'm looking forward to that time."br/]

text:
EUGENE - The unranked Oregon Ducks are at an inflection point in their highly-anticipated 2026 football season with major questions at quarterback.

Starting quarterback Dante Moore remains sidelined with a concussion injury sustained against the USC Trojans on Sept. 26. Behind him, Dylan Raiola, Brock Thomas and Akili Smith Jr. are competing for the starting job against the Nebraska Cornhuskers.

While Moore's season is on hold, the conversations around his NFL Draft stock keep moving.

Oregon entered the season ranked No. 2, with billboards in Tokyo featuring quarterback Dante Moore as part of his Heisman Trophy campaign.

The season has hardly unfolded as expected. But Oregon’s two upset losses and Moore’s injury should not all be bundled into one judgment about his NFL future.

Mel Kiper’s Dante Moore Ranking Comes With a Challenge

NFL Draft analyst Mel Kiper Jr. released his first top-25 prospect big board and included Moore on it, pushing back on the narrative that Moore has plummeted off of the NFL radar. Kiper Jr. included Moore at No. 25 overall on his first 2027 NFL Draft Big Board. Six quarterbacks landed ahead of him, including Texas’ Arch Manning at No. 24.

Before the season started, Kiper Jr. said his prediction for the No. 1 overall selection was a two-quarterback race between Moore and Manning.

Moore's NFL Draft outlook does come with one challenge from Kiper Jr.

"But he has to show he can take over some games against top-tier competition. His performance against Penn State in 2025 (at a time when the Nittany Lions were the No. 3 team in the country) was exceptional," Kiper wrote.

"But he couldn't bottle that performance and repeat it against other top teams over the rest of that season. He now has a chance to prove he can rise to the matchup this year -- most notably against Ohio State on Nov. 7," Kiper wrote.

Ohio State Matchup Looms as Dante Moore’s Return Remains Uncertain

Oregon’s looming matchup with No. 4 Ohio State in Columbus falls exactly six weeks after Moore suffered his concussion in Los Angeles.

Oregon coach Dan Lanning has not revealed a timeline for Moore's return and reiterated that the program will be very cautious, considering the severity of the injury. The good sign is that Moore is practicing for the second straight week.

If medically cleared and available, Moore could have an opportunity to change the conversation around both his draft stock and Oregon’s season. He could become the savior of the season.

The game vs. the Buckeyes might also be the Ducks' big opportunity to grab attention from the College Football Playoff committee. Oregon already has two losses, with dwindling chances at making the CFP but an upset at The Shoe would change the narrative dramatically.

For Moore, coming back this season would help show NFL evaluators how he handles pressure and executes against elite talent. Oregon faces another currently-ranked team on its schedule in No. 25 Northwestern on Halloween.

Moore was widely viewed as the early favorite to become the No. 1 quarterback selected in the 2027 NFL Draft, dominating a poll from insiders and topping Texas quarterback Arch Manning.

Notably, NFL Draft analyst Todd McShay predicted Moore would still be a top-five pick and said he's "not overrated."

So while Moore's overall dominance of potentially being the first quarterback off the board in the 2027 NFL Draft may have taken a hit, his draft stock as a whole has not crumbled. NFL scouts and personnel have flocked to Autzen Stadium this season, as the Ducks have become a strong pipeline to the league.

NFL Draft/ Quarterback Outlook

Around the sport, other quarterbacks are starting to emerge and grab attention of the NFL. Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker, Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, Miami quarterback Darian Mensah, Missouri quarterback Austin Simmons and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr now enter the conversation as potential top quarterbacks selected in the 2027 draft.

Oregon has now had at least six players taken in the NFL Draft in each of the last four years, with 31 total selections under Lanning. Oregon has 48 players across NFL rosters, practice squads and reserve lists.

Before his injury, Moore completed 69.7 percent of his passes for 926 yards, nine touchdowns and and impressive zero interceptions this season.

The Ducks host Nebraska at Autzen Stadium on Saturday night with the challenge of winning without Moore.

text:
As the Sunday games of NFL Week 6 approach, we're taking a look at the injury status of running backs Quinshon Judkins, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and TreVeyon Henderson.

Along with those three, the other running backs covered are Alvin Kamara, Rico Dowdle and Jadarian Price.

Before we get to the latest on them, the notable backs who have been ruled out include Saquon Barkley, Jeremiyah Love, Breece Hall and Kyle Monangai.

Now, here's our roundup of running back injuries for Week 6.

MORE: Josh Jacobs expected to be eligible for Week 7 return

Quinshon Judkins injury update

Cleveland Browns running back Quinshon Judkins (10) runs the ball against Chicago Bears linebacker Devin Bush (12) during the first half at Soldier Field. Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Quinshon Judkins sustained an ankle injury during the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets.

The second-year back sat out the first two days before finishing off the practice week with a limited session, which earned him the questionable tag.

Seeing that he had only one limited practice, we'd put Judkins' chances of playing at around 50/50.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt injury update

Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (22) carries the ball for a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys in the second quarter at Northwest Stadium. Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Croskey-Merritt got off to a bad start to the practice week, as he wasn't able to take part on either Thursday or Friday.

The running back known as "Bill" will have one more opportunity to get on the practice field on Saturday before the Commanders give him a designation.

For now, it looks like he's heading for a questionable tag at best.

TreVeyon Henderson injury update

New England Patriots running back Treveyon Henderson (32) warms up before the game against the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl LX at Levi's Stadium. Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

After being diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, the expectation was that Henderson wouldn't practice this week, let alone play.

However, he logged three limited practices and is listed as questionable.

"I feel pretty good. We'll see how things go," Henderson said during the week, according to Evan Lazar of Patriots.com.

MORE: Fantasy football running back rankings in Week 6

It's stunning that Henderson actually has a chance to play with what is normally a multi-week injury. We tend to lean toward him not playing, but we'll be on the lookout for a firm answer ahead of kickoff on Sunday.

Alvin Kamara injury update

New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara (41) drops a pass late in the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Credit: Matthew Hinton-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Kamara is still dealing with the back issue he picked up in Week 4.

He turned in three limited practices with the Saints this week before being given the questionable tag.

That amount of participation was actually an upgrade from last week, when he logged only two limited practices before being listed as questionable and ultimately suiting up.

MORE: Week 6 fantasy football start-sit for Pollard, Lloyd, Tuten, Marks

We predict Kamara will be active.

Rico Dowdle injury update

Pittsburgh Steelers running back Rico Dowdle (13) participates in OTA drills at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Dowdle has not taken the field for the Steelers since Week 2 because of a toe injury.

The veteran rusher saw an upgrade in participation this week after he logged two full practices, but he's still uncertain to play due to a questionable tag.

Since Dowdle did turn in those two full practices, we believe he's going to play, but there may not be a lot of work for him given how great Jaylen Warren has looked lately.

Jadarian Price injury update

Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (8) during warmups before the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field. Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Price is still on injured reserve with his chest injury, but the Seahawks running back received an encouraging update on Friday.

Head coach Mike Macdonald told Seattle Sports 710 AM that Price may be back "sooner rather than later," so it appears a Week 8 return when he is first eligible is on the table.

Price will be rejoining a crowded backfield, as fellow rusher Zach Charbonnet is expected back and Emanuel Wilson should continue seeing touches.

text:
In Week 4 of the 2025 season, Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill Tyreek Hill suffered a dislocated knee injury, which forced him to miss the remainder of the year.

The injury resulted in multiple torn ligaments and two surgeries for the All-Pro wide receiver, who, prior to his injury, was still playing at a high level. During that Week 4 game against the New York Jets, Hill was on pace for his second 100-yard game of the season despite Miami being winless during the first three games.

Through the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season, the former Dolphins receiver remains unsigned as he continues to recover from his devastating injury. Now, Hill appears closer to returning; however, an off-the-field situation may disrupt his eventual return to the NFL.

Former Miami Dolphins Wide Receiver Tyreek Hill Handed Clear Message

Tyreek Hill's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, had stated that Hill might sign with an NFL team within the next few weeks. That was before Hill's civil trial verdict on Tuesday.

Regarding the verdict, The Athletic's Adam Kilgore wrote: "In a civil trial verdict Tuesday evening, a Miami jury found Hill liable for two counts of battery against his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill, and awarded her $500,000 in compensatory damages. Tyreek Hill, 32, was found not liable for eight other domestic abuse-related counts and did not have to pay punitive damages."

Kilgore discussed how that might affect his NFL return, as he wrote: "It's unclear whether the NFL will weigh the new revelations in any potential discipline against Hill. The league does not discuss specifics of ongoing investigations.

The NFL will consider all evidence its investigators can gather about Hill's current case, including speaking with Hill himself. The league levies any punishment when its investigation concludes, regardless of a player's free-agent or injury status. But it can place a free agent on the commissioner's exempt list if he signs with a team while under NFL investigation. One recent example is cornerback Terrion Arnold, who cannot play or practice with the Seattle Seahawks, who signed him after the Detroit Lions cut him in the aftermath of kidnapping charges against him.

Any team that signs Hill would have to weigh his ability against several factors: his health, potential public backlash, time he might spend on the exempt list and the length of a possible suspension if the NFL finds he violated the personal conduct policy. It will not be simple for teams to consider what Hill might provide. For the NFL, it never has been."

Tyreek Hill's NFL Return

Hill's off-the-field situation only complicates his potential NFL return. Unlike years past, when the Miami Dolphins sent a significant trade package to the Kansas City Chiefs to acquire the wide receiver, Hill is an aging player who has not produced a 1,000-yard season since 2023 and is coming off a career-altering knee injury.

After Hill's verdict, Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that nothing was imminent on Hill signing with an NFL team. He said, "Nothing is imminent at this time. He's continuing his rehab with the goal of being on a team in the immediate future."

Rosenhaus had previously expressed that several teams were interested in Hill, but that may have changed after Tuesday's verdict.

FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is likely to be activated Saturday after missing the past four games with a right high ankle sprain, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

The Patriots have an open spot on their 53-man roster, and activating Brown adds a premium pass-catching option for quarterback Drake Maye, starting with Sunday's home game against the New York Jets.

In anticipation of Brown's return, Maye compared the situation to basketball.

"I think you see it in the NBA; it's probably the closest thing that I can think of," Maye said earlier this week. "When they start doubling the best player once they get past half court, then they're just leaving a corner 3 open or leaving a guy open for a dunk. So it's kind of like playing receiver with a guy like that.

"We've got a lot of guys that have made plays now, so it's going to be tough on defenses. But I know we've got a tough challenge this week, so looking forward to it."

Brown sustained the injury early in the third quarter of the season opener Sept. 9. He returned to practice for the first time Wednesday and said coach Mike Vrabel would ultimately decide when he plays, noting a key consideration would be for the "long haul, not just for temporarily."

Brown was limited throughout the week of practice, according to the Patriots' injury report, and he will likely be eased back into the mix before taking on his usual heavy workload.

The New England Patriots offense could get a major boost this week. The team will likely activate star wide receiver A.J. Brown off Injured Reserve to play against the New York Jets on Sunday, according to the NFL Network.

Brown suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and has missed four weeks so far, the minimum required when a team places any player on IR. The three-time Pro Bowler returned to practice this week, but was limited all three days. His official game designation is questionable.

The WR had just three receptions on four targets for 26 yards before going down against the Seattle Seahawks in the Super Bowl rematch season opener.

The Patriots offense was rocky to start the season, with quarterback Drake Maye struggling with forcing passes and committing turnovers. Their biggest offensive struggle came against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3, as they failed to get into the end zone and lost 35-6.

Without Brown, the worry was that the Patriots couldn't march down the field without a true WR1. Maye's capabilities were called into question, with many wondering whether last year's near-MVP season was a fluke.

Despite his absence, the Maye and Co. have seemed to get it together and have increased production tenfold. They look like a team to beat over the last two weeks, having defeated the Buffalo Bills 29-26 and the Las Vegas Raiders 45-17. The Patriots are currently 10th in passing yards (1,274), but tied for most interceptions (7).

Brown returning should elevate the offense, finally give fans a look at what a Maye-Brown offense looks like, and continue the upward trajectory.

text:
The rest of the NFL Week 6 slate is nearly upon us and we're going around the league to check out the latest injury updates on DJ Moore, A.J. Brown, Chris Olave, Mike Evans and more wide receivers whose statues are in doubt.

Before we get to those players, Rashee Rice is the most notable wide receiver who has been ruled out for Week 6.

As far as the wide receivers who have been cleared to play are concerned, the list is populated by DeVonta Smith, Zay Flowers, Ladd McConkey, Denzel Boston, KC Concepcion, Dontayvion Wicks and Quentin Johnston.

Now, a look at what we know about Moore, Brown, Olave, Evans and more wide receivers who are uncertain for this week.

MORE: Fantasy football wide receiver rankings for Week 6

DJ Moore injury update

Buffalo Bills wide receiver DJ Moore #2 runs after making a catch during the first quarter against the New England Patriots at New Highmark Stadium. Credit: Mark Konezny-Imagn via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

DJ Moore is still trying to get past his AC joint sprain that he suffered in Week 2 and re-aggravated in Week 4.

After not playing in Week 5, Moore was only able to log a single limited practice in Week 6 and is questionable to suit up.

Buffalo Bills beat reporter, Sal Capaccio of WGR 550, believes the Bills will hold Moore out with the bye week coming in order to try and get him right.

MORE: Fantasy football running back rankings in Week 6

We tend to agree that's what Buffalo will do.

A.J. Brown injury update

New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown (1) is tended to by trainers after injuring his ankle during the third quarter against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

UPDATE: After this article was written, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Brown "will likely" be activated off injured reserve and play in Week 6.

"The Patriots will likely activate WR AJ Brown off Injured Reserve to play against the Jets on Sunday, sources say," Rapoport reported. "Brown returned to practice this week after a stint on IR with a high-ankle sprain and now an anticipated return to the field."

Now, it'll be interesting to see if Brown will be on a limited snap count in his first game back after more than a month off. Be on the lookout for any report about that between now and Sunday afternoon.

END OF UPDATE

A.J. Brown has been working his way back from a high-ankle sprain since Week 1.

Initially given a timeline of about six weeks, according to reports, it appears Brown is ahead of schedule, but he only turned in limited practices this week after being designated to return from injured reserve, picking up the questionable tag for Week 6.

We find it hard to believe Brown is going to return off only limited practices, so we expect the New England Patriots wideout to sit.

MORE: Fantasy football quarterback rankings for Week 6

A decision is expected to come down on Saturday, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Chris Olave injury update

New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) looks on from the sideline in the second quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Chris Olave draws the questionable tag for Week 6, but because of an illness, not because of an injury.

Olave didn't practice on Wednesday and Thursday before taking part in a limited session on Friday, so he's trending toward suiting up.

We'd say Olave is likely to play because illness rarely keeps players from playing, especially when the illness occurs early in the week like it did for the New Orleans Saints wideout.

Mike Evans injury update

San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) during the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium. Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Mike Evans overcame a rib injury to play last week, but now has an Achilles issue added.

The veteran wideout has been sidelined at practice over the first two days as a result. He was, however, spotted doing rehab work on the side field, NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco reported, so there's hope.

Evans has one more practice on Saturday before he draws a tag for Week 6. It looks like a questionable tag is in his future, but Maiocco believes Evans will ultimately suit up.

Stefon Diggs injury update

Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs (3) catches a four-yard pass for a touchdown thrown by quarterback Jayden Daniels (not pictured) against the Dallas Cowboys during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

After not practicing at all last week before being ruled out with his hamstring injury, Stefon Diggs started off this week with a "DNP" on Thursday before he was upgraded on Friday.

That has Diggs moving in a positive direction, but we still need to see what he does on Saturday.

For now, Diggs looks like he's headed toward a questionable tag.

DK Metcalf injury update

Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf (4) scores a touchdown in the third quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Acrisure Stadium. Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

DK Metcalf popped up on the Pittsburgh Steelers' injury report on Friday with an illness and is now questionable to play.

Illnesses aren't usually a cause for concern for a player's status, but it's a bit different in this instance because Metcalf picked his up at the end of the week.

Hopefully there will be some clarity on Metcalf on Saturday, but if not we'll know no later than 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, when the Steelers release their list of inactives.
