The assigned game participation statuses to six players on Friday ahead of their Week 6 home game against the New Orleans Saints. That is the most injury designations the Giants have had this season.

Tight end Theo Johnson (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck) and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) have all been declared out for the contest.

Johnson’s absence means Thomas Fidone II, who has been a healthy scratch through the first four games of the season before finally getting a suit last week, will see a larger role on offense this Sunday.

“Oh, he could help us. He could help us,” head coach John Harbaugh said of Fidone. “He’s had great practices, runs good routes, and played well on special teams last week. Thomas is ready to play, as he showed last week.”

Johnson’s status is also worth monitoring in future weeks, given that he went from a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being kept out of practice on Friday.

The Giants are getting safety Jason Pinnock back for the week after he missed last week due to a concussion.

Pinnock appeared to have quietly passed Nubin on the depth chart for a starting job, but the concussion he suffered two weeks ago gave Nubin a mulligan last week.

Three key Giants are listed as questionable for Sunday: both starting offensive tackles, Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and Andrew Thomas (groin), and starting outside linebacker Abdul Carter (calf).

All three were limited in practice Friday, an upgrade after they were held out Wednesday and Thursday. The feeling is that both tackles should be good to go for Sunday. If not, rookie J.C. Davis will get the nod at left tackle, where he played well in the preseason, and Marcus Mbow will start at right tackle.

Carter’s status is also worth monitoring. He’s been a big part of the defensive pass rush. With the Giants already missing Brian Burns for the rest of the season due to an ACL injury, not having Carter would be a huge blow to a pass rush that has started to click over the last couple of weeks.

text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Quarterback Caleb Williams was officially listed as questionable on the Chicago Bears' final injury report ahead of their Week 6 game at the Atlanta Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, Fox).

Williams was a full participant during the Bears' Wednesday walk-through and practice sessions Thursday and Friday. The quarterback said he had to go through "a bunch of medical protocols" before being cleared by team trainers, which could happen before the team leaves for Atlanta.

"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Bears coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "He looked good [Thursday] for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. Part of the plan, and he's on track right now."

text:

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled of Sunday’s AFC North opener against the Cleveland Browns, coach Jesse Minter said Friday.

It’s the second straight game Jackson will miss. He was sidelined for Sunday’s win over the Atlanta Falcons and hasn’t practiced since he sprained an ankle in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Minter on Wednesday called Jackson “definitely day-to-day.”

With Jackson unavailable, backup Tyler Huntley will make his second straight start and third in the Ravens’ past eight games, dating to the end of last season. Huntley went 24-for-32 for 201 yards and two touchdowns and had a rushing touchdown as he helped lead the Ravens’ comeback in Atlanta.

“He’s a really good player,” Minter said of Huntley, who’s 6-6 as a Ravens starter over six seasons. “And he’s got a great demeanor. And he’s got great poise. He’s got great respect amongst his teammates. ... He’s just got a cool, calm, collected, confident [demeanor]. To me, that’s infectious. And, when he’s in there, that’s kind of how the guys feel. And it’s really no different with Lamar.”

Center Cam Jurgens, who was in line to make his Ravens debut after being acquired in a trade last week, is one of three other Ravens ruled out. Minter indicated Friday that Jurgens remains in the NFL’s concussion protocol. He was limited in practice this week while he wore a red, noncontact pinnie.

Rookie Vega Ioane is expected to make his third straight start at center. That will leave another hole at right guard, where Emery Jones Jr. (ankle) and Andrew Vorhees (foot) are questionable for Sunday’s game. Both were limited in practice this week.

“We have a ton of confidence in the offensive line that we’ll put out there,” Minter said. “And then we’ll be super excited when he [Jurgens] gets a chance to join the lineup.”

Rookie tight end Matt Hibner and defensive lineman Broderick Washington will also miss Sunday’s game. Hibner hurt his left hand against the Falcons, missed practice this week and watched Friday’s session while wearing a cast and street clothes. Hibner, who has five catches for 70 yards and a touchdown and has played 42.7% of the team’s offensive snaps, is not expected to miss much time, Minter said.

Washington hurt his ankle late in the third quarter Sunday and did not return. He was limited in practice Wednesday and was sidelined Thursday and Friday. He’s played a third of the team’s defensive snaps.

Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson, who hasn’t played since Week 3 because of an operation on a broken finger, is expected to return Sunday. He was a full participant in all three practices this week, and Minter said there’s little risk of reinjury. Hendrickson said after practice Thursday that the team was still deciding on how he would protect his hand.

“I’m excited for him to be feeling better,” Minter said. “I think we’ll get a chance to see what he can bring to our defense.”

Rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane, who hasn’t played since suffering a Week 1 wrist injury, had a “great week,” Minter said, but was listed as questionable for Week 6. The third-round pick was a full participant in practice this week and is expected to be activated off injured reserve ahead of Sunday’s game.

The Browns ruled out five players, including backup running back Dylan Sampson. Starting running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle), starting defensive lineman Mason Graham (knee/ankle) and starting linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) are questionable. Starting rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion, who was knocked out of the Browns’ loss Sunday to the New York Jets, cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play Sunday.

text:
The announcement that Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss time to deal with a blood clot left PFT’s Mike Florio with many unanswered questions.

Last Friday, Hurts suddenly appeared on the Eagles’ injury report with a calf injury, but he fully participated in practice. He played in the team’s 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday and, by all accounts, was expected to play this upcoming Sunday against the Carolina Panthers.

“It was a very unique experience, to say the least,” said Hurts in a mid-week press conference when asked about the injury. “I don’t want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game.”

However, on Thursday, the team announced that Hurts would miss the Panthers game because of a blood clot in his leg. Per the statement, the quarterback visited the training room last Thursday, saying he was “cleated” during the previous Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. He received treatment, practiced Friday, flew with the team to London, and participated in Saturday’s walkthrough. After the walkthrough, the team said Hurts underwent an ultrasound “out of an abundance of caution,” which “revealed a superficial blood clot.”

Florio was openly curious about the injury before the team fully announced that it was a blood clot. He and Chris Simms questioned how the situation was being handled and its potential impact on bettors.

“The whole thing just seems odd to me,” said Florio on Thursday’s episode of PFT Live. “I hope somebody is trying to figure out more what happened.”

“It is odd,” added Simms. “I understand the approach by the Eagles and all of that. I get it. You know, we talk about that stuff all the time, the competitive advantages. You don’t want to do that. But yet, yes, it’s fishy.”

Simms then ranted on how the lack of information about Hurts’ injury may have impacted the way bettors approached the Eagles-Jaguars game, and how they might be due some kind of payback or voiding of bets because the Eagles and NFL were not upfront about the injury situation despite knowing before the game about Hurts’s condition.

“We don’t know what would have happened if he was healthy,” continued Simms. “That’s where this has to start going with these injury reports and stuff. Bets void if we find out a week later. It’s void. We pay you back even though you lost the game because you weren’t given the right information, even though we told you you were and we made you bet your money.”

After Florio noted that some kind of regulation around sports gambling was likely to happen if Democrats take control of Congress, he brought it back to the issue at hand.

“As it relates to the NFL’s injury report, it is so bare-bones. There would be no suggestion that the Eagles failed to comply,” said Florio. “Now, my question is, should he have been downgraded to questionable at some point?”

Florio and Simms caught a lot of flak on social media for the perception that they put gamblers’ needs ahead of the health of NFL players like Hurts. On Friday’s show, Florio responded to those criticisms, calling out the NFL’s double standard: encouraging people to bet on its games while not providing the fullest picture possible.

“Let me just be clear on this because apparently there are some folks out there on social media who took exception to the fact that Chris and I were making the case on behalf of people who wager their hard-earned money that they are kept in the dark,” said Florio. “That there is inside information out there, that it isn’t available in full and fairly transparent ways to the people who are expected to plunk down their money. And we didn’t know he had a blood clot at the time we said it, but I still believe what we said yesterday. And there are ways to be concerned about Jalen Hurts from a health standpoint and make the point that these injuries are hidden, that the information isn’t shared with the individuals who are out there deciding on the menu of many different wagers where they’re going to put their hard-earned money that they are likely to lose sooner or later.”

But you would think, when you read that statement, at some point over the weekend, aren’t you going to downgrade Jalen Hurts to questionable?”

On PFT, Florio brought the conversation back to the NFL and the Eagles’ decision not to be more transparent about what they knew the day before the Eagles-Jaguars game.

Given that the Eagles specifically said the team had “remained in communication with the league office,” we asked the league office whether it had anything to add — specifically as to the question of why Hurts’s status for the game wasn’t changed at any time to “questionable.”

… Given that, between Saturday and Tuesday, the blood clot moved (making Hurts unavailable for Week 6), it would have been appropriate for the public to know that there was a possibility that, between Saturday and the start of Sunday’s game, the blood clot could move, or Hurts’s condition could otherwise deteriorate.

And, yes, it’s possible to have genuine concern for the player’s health while also pointing out the flaws in the current rules that work to the disadvantage of the betting public. Every injury necessarily represents a negative impact on the player’s health. The question becomes whether or not there is sufficient transparency.

Darius Slayton’s short run in Indianapolis has come to an end.

The Colts announced Friday they released the veteran receiver they signed in late September for another option at wideout after Alec Pierce hit injury reserve with a heel issue.

The Colts had hoped Slayton’s familiarity with quarterback Daniel Jones from several seasons together with the Giants would make him a downfield threat with Pierce out.

In his handful of weeks as a Colt, Slayton did not see the field.

Slayton, 29, spent seven seasons with the Giants after they selected him in the fifth round of the 2019 NFL Draft, where he averaged 15.0 yards per catch on 296 career receptions with 4,435 total yards.

He led the Giants in receiving yards in 2022 and 2023, but his production gradually declined for Big Blue until his release, even with Malik Nabers missing much of the 2025 season.

Slayton was partially hindered by double sports hernias last season, which he underwent surgery for on April 30.

His tenure with the Giants came to an end with his Sept. 7 release.

“Grateful for my time in NY,” he posted to X. “7 years a Giant nothing but love for one of the most prestigious organizations in the NFL. Excited to see what’s next.’’

Slayton suffered a knee injury at the end of last week’s Colts practices that kept him out of Indianapolis’ lineup in Week 5.

Head coach Shane Steichen said this week Slayton’s injury had “gotten better.”

The Colts have been thin at receiver to start the season.

Aside from Pierce, Ashton Dulin has dealt with a hamstring injury and Keenan Allen missed the Colts’ contest with the Commanders in London in Week 4.

text:
"I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," coach Ben Johnson said Friday before practice. "He looked good yesterday for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through. He went through his own throwing session beforehand — part of the plan — and he's on track right now."

Williams told reporters Thursday that "the other day" he was timed at "one of my high speeds I've ever hit, and so I can move, I can run, I've got strength."

"It probably is a little bit different intensity [in a game]," Johnson said, "and yet that's what we're trying to work through here over the course of the week is just getting him up to those high speeds and making sure that we don't have any effects that continue to linger on. Once again, we're right on track with the plan and we'll see what it looks like, see how he feels.

"Confidence is a big part of it as well, but I know he wants to play. He's a competitor. It's been not fun for him the last few weeks watching from the sideline, just like any guy that loves football. It's been a tough deal for him. I know he's itching to get back out there and help us win ball games. If we feel really good as a front office, a coaching staff and player himself about playing, then we'll go ahead and go with it."

If Williams cannot play Sunday, Johnson declined to disclose whether Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum would be the Bears' starting quarterback.

"We have two guys that are equally qualified," Johnson said.

Like Williams, cornerback Kyler Gordon was a full participant in practice all week and is questionable for Sunday's game. The Bears have until next week to activate Gordon from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list, where he has been since before training camp began due to a calf injury.

"He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far," Johnson said. "I do feel good about him [playing], whether that's this week or next week. I do feel good about him being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far."

Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is also questionable with a hip injury he sustained last weekend against the Packers that limited him in practice all week.

Bears players who have been ruled out of Sunday's contest are running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo (quadriceps) and linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quadriceps).

Monangai will miss his second straight game.

"It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR," Johnson said. "It's still week-to-week, and as far as I know, he's trending in the right direction."

The Bears will be missing their two starting defensive ends in Odeyingbo and Montez Sweat, who is suspended by the NFL for the next two games.

Defensive lineman Shemar Turner, a 2025 second-round pick, was activated Tuesday from the PUP list and could play for the first time since tearing his ACL in Week 8 of last season against the Ravens.

"What showed up in his college tape was the violence with which he played," Johnson said. "He's got an aggressive demeanor about him. Despite the injuries that have held him back, training camp last year, ACL, all these things, hopeful that that part comes out. He's very similar to a lot of these guys that we're bringing in. They love football, and so being out there on the grass competing, that's really where they come to life the most. So, I'm excited to see him go out there and compete."

Without Edwards, the Bears will be without the individual who relays play calls from the coaching staff to the rest of the huddle.

"What you feel from T.J., certainly during practice and then during games, is just the communication aspect," Johnson said. "Everyone's going to know exactly what's going on, where to line up. He's going to be quick and decisive with the calls, and he never panics. And so, when you have a new voice, that's where it takes a second for the unit to understand and get the rhythm.

"We've been facing that on offense the last few weeks with different quarterbacks in the huddle and cadence. It's no different for the 'green dot' there on defense, maybe not to the same extent. And yet, there's that level of poise and communication aspect that goes a long way. A lot of plays are won before the snap even happens, and that's what I think those green dots help bring to the table. And so you miss a guy like T.J. He's been a Steady Eddie, and he's played really dependable football, really through his tenure here. But it gives an opportunity for other guys to step up and make an impact themselves. Good thing we have some depth in that linebacker room. We have a lot of guys that have played a lot of ball at a high level and won meaningful games for us."

Offensive tackle Ozzy Trapilo, meanwhile, continues to make strides as he rebounds from a knee injury he suffered in last season's wild card playoff win over Green Bay. Johnson revealed that "there's a chance" that Trapilo is active Sunday for the first time this season. He was initially expected to miss all or most of the year but returned to practice Aug. 16, much earlier than anticipated.

Final injury reports are in for NFL Week 6, and the injury landscape is an absolute minefield. Superstars are banged up across the board, which drastically alters NFL odds, point spreads, and player props.

The Philadelphia Eagles have a staggering 24 players listed on their injury report, including QB1 Jalen Hurts (blood clot). Meanwhile, the Washington Commanders and Baltimore Ravens are dealing with 21 names each.

When rosters are this battered, it violently shifts the field position battle and forces defensive schemes to adjust on the fly.

These absences present unique opportunities to find value in total points and replacement-player props. Let’s dive into the Week 6 injury landscape to uncover exactly how these situations impact the board and where I am finding the smartest betting angles.

NFL Week 6 Injury Report: Star Player Statuses & Betting Impact

Keeping track of who is in and who is out is the fastest way to gain an edge at the sportsbook. This week, the injury report is littered with franchise quarterbacks, elite pass-catchers, and workhorse running backs.

Here is a roundup of the latest injury statuses for the league’s top stars heading into Week 6.

Key Line Movers to Watch

In the modern NFL, only a handful of players have the power to drastically shift point spreads and moneylines. When betting into this week’s slate, pay special attention to the following situations.

Lamar Jackson, QB, Baltimore Ravens

Jackson is out with an ankle issue, totally reshaping the betting outlook for Baltimore’s road matchup against the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens opened as heavy 6.5-point favorites with a -275 moneyline.

Without his elite pocket presence and ability to extend third down conversions, the best-available spread crashed to Ravens -3. Their moneyline also plummeted to -168.

This absence fundamentally alters Baltimore’s offensive ceiling. It significantly lowers their red zone efficiency against standard defensive sets, making the Browns an intriguing look. Check the NFL starting QB odds market for updates on backup valuations.

Tyler Huntley will assume the starting role. The former Browns quarterback (in preseason) has two starts against Cleveland, going 1-1 with a touchdown and an interception. His most impressive outing came in relief of Jackson, though, as he threw for 270 yards and a touchdown in a furious failed comeback attempt in 2021.

Jalen Hurts, QB & Saquon Barkley, RB, Philadelphia Eagles

Already missing Saquon Barkley, the Eagles opened as slight favorites against the Panthers. But then things went from bad to worse when Jalen Hurts was diagnosed with blood-clot issues that will keep him out indefinitely.

Once news broke that Hurts would miss this contest, bettors pounded Panthers. The best-available spread moved to Panthers -3.5. The Eagles’ moneyline flipped from a near pick ’em (-103) to +147 underdogs.

Without their primary offensive weapons, Philadelphia’s offense will struggle to sustain drives, negatively impacting their turnover differential and time of possession.

Tanner McKee will get the start in Hurts’ place. The Stanford product has two NFL starts to his name, along with five passing touchdowns and one interception. He is 1-1.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Mayfield’s thumb injury is a massive red flag for a throwing hand. He did not practice, and he will miss yet another game. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point road favorites against the Buccaneers.

Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start for the Bucs. After a less-than-ideal first start, Daniels had a clean 212 total yards and a touchdown en route to an upset win on TNF last week. Daniels nearly doubled his passer rating (65.0 to 110.2) and guided the Bucs to their first win of the season.

text:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup.

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field.

Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons.

He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set.

While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability.

"I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time.

There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley.

"There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down."

Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

text:
The NFL keeps chugging along, and as with every upcoming slate, injuries have become a central focus. Unlike previous weeks, where it feels like it's been more about who is out of the lineup rather than who is in it, Week 6 is more of a mixed bag on the injury front, which can be looked at as a glass half full.

However, if you're a Ravens fan, you're certainly not ecstatic about the latest injury developments as Lamar Jackson is slated to miss his second-straight game due to an ankle injury. That means Tyler Huntley will get another start after defeating the Falcons last Sunday night. Meanwhile, the Eagles are drowning in injury news and will also be starting a backup quarterback in Tanner McKee. This comes after the revelation that starter Jalen Hurts is dealing with a blood clot in his calf. He headlines what is a CVS receipt-sized injury list for Philadelphia this season.

But, as we mentioned, it's not all doom and gloom from an injury standpoint. Michael Penix Jr. (rib) has the green light to play for the Falcons, while it's not out of the realm of possibility that Caleb Williams makes his return to the Bears or A.J. Brown reinserts himself into the Patriots offense this week, either.

Below, we'll run through every injury report across the league as we barrel towards Week 6.

Note: Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami, and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.

Texans at Jaguars (in London)

Texans: WR Tank Dell (knee), S Jalen Pitre (shoulder), RB David Montgomery (groin) OUT; S Ja'Marcus Ingram (elbow), LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) QUESTIONABLE.

Jaguars: CB Montaric Brown (hamstring), LS Ross Matiscik (shoulder) OUT; CB Jaylon Jones (hamstring) QUESTIONABLE

David Montgomery did not make the trip to London and has since officially been ruled out. That means backup Woody Marks will see the lion's share of the touches out of the Texans' backfield. Meanwhile, safety Jalen Pitre did not practice all week with a shoulder injury, so it's not surprising to see him ruled out. As for Ingram and To'oTo'o, they both practiced fully on both Thursday and Friday and seem more on the probable side of the questionable designation.

The Jaguars will once again be without their top long snapper as they ruled out Ross Matiscik due to a shoulder injury he suffered last week against the Eagles. However, they did have some reinforcements after signing Jacob Bobenmoyer.

Bears at Falcons

Bears: LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring), LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad), RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe), DL Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) OUT; QB Caleb Williams (hamstring), DB Tyrique Stevenson Sr. (hip), DB Kyler Gordon (calf) QUESTIONABLE

Falcons: CB C.J. Henderson (groin) OUT; DE Za'Darius Smith (neck)

Caleb Williams was a full participant throughout the week of practice, but is officially questionable to make his return in Week 6. On Thursday, Williams told reporters he does "not know if I'm playing yet."

Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) was a full participant in practice on Friday and carries no injury designation, so the Falcons starter will play in Week 6 against Chicago. Atlanta won't have corner C.J. Henderson, however, as he's still dealing with a groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Ravens.

Ravens at Browns

Ravens: QB Lamar Jackson (ankle), C Cam Jurgens (concussion), TE Matt Hibner (hand), DT Broderick Washington (ankle) OUT; G Emery Jones Jr. (ankle), WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) QUESTIONABLE

Baltimore will be without Lamar Jackson for the second straight week as he continues to deal with an ankle injury. The two-time NFL MVP has yet to practice since suffering the injury, and his absence will thrust backup Tyler Huntley into the starting role yet again. Meanwhile, Jurgens will miss Sunday's divisional matchup as he is still in concussion protocol. That'll likely result in Vega Ioane starting at center. On the bright side, Zay Flowers is good to go as he carries no injury designation after being limited on Thursday and Friday with a toe injury.

Cleveland saw Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Carson Schwesinger all return to practice on Friday in a limited capacity after missing the start of the week due to injury. They are each questionable to play, but that return to the field does leave the door open for them to play in Week 6.

Titans at Colts

Titans: DL Jordan Elliott (not injury-related), S Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) OUT; RB Tyjae Spears (knee), CB Joshua Williams (pec) QUESTIONABLE

Colts: LB Jaylon Carlies (ribs), WR Ashton Dulin (hamstring) OUT; TE Will Mallory (thumb), TE Tyler Warren (groin) QUESTIONABLE

Spears returned to practice on Friday as a full participant after missing Thursday's session as he manages a knee injury. Cornerback Joshua Williams was also a full participant Friday, despite his questionable status.

The most notable development with Indianapolis is Tyler Warren. The tight end popped up on the injury report on Friday as a limited participant due to a groin injury and is now questionable for Sunday.

Jets at Patriots

Jets: RB Breece Hall (quad), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle), OL Dylan Parham (knee) OUT; S Dane Belton (knee), WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle), TE Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) QUESTIONABLE

It'll be another week without Breece Hall in the Jets backfield as he continues to deal with a quad injury. That means Braelon Allen will continue to get the bulk of the work in the running game. However, New York will get first-round rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. back in the fold. Despite being listed as questionable, he is slated to make his return, logging a full practice on Friday.

The Patriots will get No. 1 corner Christian Gonzalez back after he had been sidelined with a shoulder injury. Gonzalez was a full participant over the past two days and does not carry an injury designation. Elsewhere on the report, all eyes will be on A.J. Brown, who is officially questionable. After suffering a high ankle sprain in the season opener, Brown is eligible to come off injured reserve this week and was limited throughout the week. Will Campbell and TreVeyon Henderson are also questionable after limited participation at practice.

Saints: LB Kaden Wlliss (calf), LB Anfernee Jennings (knee) OUT; RB Alvin Kamara (back), WR Chris Olave (illness), DT Nathan Shepherd (illness), CB Lorenzo Styles (knee), LS Zach Wood (calf) QUESTIONABLE

Olave and Shepherd both returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday after they were held out on Wednesday and Thursday due to illness. They are questionable, along with running back Alvin Kamara, who was limited throughout the week due to a back injury.

New York couldn't get Hood, Johnson, or Nubin on the field on Friday and have thus been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against New Orleans. Meanwhile, Abdul Carter, Jermaine Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas all returned to practice on Friday in a limited capacity after missing the first two days. Moton was a full participant at practice this week, so the Panthers tackle should be looked at as probable for this Week 6 matchup, but will need to be activated in order to play. Meanwhile, outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was upgraded to a full participant on Friday, so he appears good to go, despite the questionable designation. As for Freeling, the offensive tackle was limited on Thursday and Friday, but was still listed as doubtful.

Philadelphia had already ruled out starting quarterback Jalen Hurts due to a blood clot in his calf, but the Eagles will now also be down another key pillar of the offense in Saquon Barkley. The star back will be sidelined for Week 6 due to a hamstring injury. With Barkley and Shipley hurt, Dameon Pierce will likely see the lion's share of work on the ground. On a more positive note, Tanner McKee, who is slated to start for Hurts under center, will have DeVonta Smith back in the fold. The star receiver has no injury designation after dealing with hamstring and toe injuries.

Steelers at Buccaneers

Steelers: WR Roman Wilson (finger), WR Ben Skowronik (calf), S DeShon Elliot (knee) OUT; CB Jalen Ramsey (wrist), WR DK Metcalf (illness), DT Keeanu Benton (ankle), CB Jamel Dean (ankle), RB Rico Dowdle (toe) QUESTIONABLE

DK Metcalf was a late-week addition to the injury report for Pittsburgh, which listed the wideout as a non-participant during Friday's practice due to an illness. He is officially questionable. This comes as the Steelers will already be without fellow receiver Roman Wilson, who has been ruled out with a finger injury. Meanwhile, corner Jalen Ramsey logged back-to-back limited practices to finish the week, while running back Rico Dowdle was a full participant on Thursday and Friday. Both are questionable.

Baker Mayfield will not make his return this week as he did not practice once and has since been ruled out, meaning Jalon Daniels will get his third-straight start. Defensively, the Bucs will be down a key pillar in Antoine Winfield Jr., as he continues to deal with a rib injury.

Arizona will be without its first-round rookie running back, Jeremiyah Love, as he is dealing with a left ankle injury. While it's positive that head coach Matt LaFleur noted Friday that injured reserve has not been discussed for Love, he won't be available this week against the Rams. In his place, Tyler Allgeier should see an uptick in work out of the Cardinals backfield.

Los Angeles' final injury report is short, but it does feature some notable names. That includes star corner Trent McDuffie, who did not participate on Friday due to a groin injury. Safety Kam Curl was also downgraded to a non-participant on Friday after being limited on Thursday with an ankle injury.

text:
Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love will miss Sunday's game against the host Los Angeles Rams as he continues to nurse an injured left ankle, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday.

Love did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Friday's injury report will be released Friday afternoon.

LaFleur said there haven't been discussions of putting Love on injured reserve to allow him to rest the ankle. LaFleur said that Love playing Sunday "wouldn't be in the best interest of him" and added that Love would be reevaluated Monday.

LaFleur said that he knew Monday that Love would get Wednesday off to rest and that the plan was to reassess on Wednesday, but the coach said he knew all along that Sunday was a "long shot."

While LaFleur said Love is "doing good," there hasn't been much progress on the ankle injury.

"We felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "At that point, it's like, if it's not improving, it's getting a little bit worse, we got to do what's right for the player."

LaFleur said the first time the injury could been "visually" evident was during Arizona's loss at the New York Giants, when trainers were seen working on Love's ankle. But he said the way Love plays makes it all the more important for him to get his ankle right.

"He cuts hard," LaFleur said. "That's a superpower of his. When he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right, so he can go out and perform the way that he wants. So, he can go out and, honestly, run the routes that he wants. To run routes and separate, you got to be able to put those feet in the ground and it's got to be deliberate, so we want to get him healed so he can do that in the pass game and in the run game."

Starting with the potential return of two of the Patriots biggest stars, Brown opened his 21-day window by returning to practice on Wednesday and is eligible to return from injured reserve after a four-game absence. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain 30 snaps into his Patriots debut in the season opener vs. the Seahawks. After an abrupt ending to his highly anticipated Patriots debut, Brown deferred to head coach Mike Vrabel on whether he will return this week.

"It felt pretty good. It's one step at a time with me," Brown said about his return to practice. "It's definitely still up in the air. Obviously, it's going to be Coach Vrabel's decision to see where I'm at and make the better decision for the long haul."

Although head coach Mike Vrabel said he will take it one week at a time, New England playing two games in five days with little practice time between Sunday's game vs. the Jets and Thursday night's contest vs. the Bears could factor into Brown's return. The Patriots also still have wideouts Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III, and Kyle Williams, all of whom contributed to New England's 45-point performance vs. the Raiders last week. On Friday, Vrabel was asked if he'd made a final decision on whether Brown will play Sunday against New York.

"We won't make that decision until tomorrow," Vrabel said on Brown's status. "I try to see where his conditioning level is and see where he may feel here after practice today."

As for Gonzalez, the Patriots top cornerback is expected to return to the lineup after he told reporters, "I'm good now. Ready for Sunday," earlier this week. Gonzalez is likely to return from a two-game absence after suffering a shoulder injury in the Pats Week 3 loss to the Jaguars. Gonzalez finished the game, but said adrenaline carried him through and his shoulder injury flared up once the team returned from Jacksonville.

"At that point, you got a lot of adrenaline. Adrenaline covers a lot of things in this sport. At that time, I felt good. Things happen, so it is what it is and I'm ready for this week," said Gonzalez.

With Gonzalez returning, the Pats cornerback will likely face-off against Jets WR Garrett Wilson for the fourth time in this best-on-best division rivalry. In the previous three matchups, Gonzalez held Wilson to eight catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on 51 routes covering the Jets wideout. Without starter Carlton Davis for the third time in four games, the Patriots will likely lean on Gonzalez, CB Charles Woods, NCB Marcus Jones, and fourth-corner Kindle Vildor.

There's some hope that the Patriots will get Brown and Gonzalez back this week while there's also optimism that starting LT Will Campbell (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) avoided major injuries in last Sunday's game vs. the Raiders. Initial reports said Campbell and Henderson would likely miss game time, but the two 2025 draft picks were, somewhat surprisingly, limited participants in all three practices this week.

With Campbell, the Pats left tackle said that his knee sprain isn't as serious as the one he suffered last season. As mentioned, reports suggested Campbell would miss games with the injury, but his practice participation and questionable status suggest the second-year pro could play on Sunday. If he can't play, the Pats will likely turn to first-rounder Caleb Lomu at left tackle, who played the final 43 snaps after Campbell left last week's blowout win over the Raiders.

Lomu, who played left tackle in college, allowed just one quarterback pressure on 29 pass-blocking snaps in Week 5. The rookie was more uneven as a run blocker, allowing a stuffed run while playing jumbo tight end, but Lomu was solid overall against the Raiders. The Patriots appear to have a serviceable option in Lomu to fill in for their starting left tackle, which could factor into the decision to play Campbell if he's less than 100 percent.

With their first-round pick from the 2025 draft's status unknown, New England's second-rounder from the same rookie class, Henderson, also seemed to have dodged the injury bullet. Initial reports indicated Henderson was headed for a multi-week absence with a high-ankle sprain, the same injury that landed Brown on injured reserve. Instead, Henderson was a limited participant in all three practices this week and has a chance to play on Sunday.

Along with Henderson, the Patriots have lead-back Rhamondre Stevenson and third-string RB Cory Kiner on the active roster. New England could also elevate second-year RB Lan Larison or recently signed practice-squad RB Hassan Haskins as depth. If one of their two practice-squad running backs is elevated on Saturday, that'll indicate Henderson might sit out Sunday's game. Still, it's encouraging that he's practicing following his injury scare.

The rest of the Patriots questionable starters have been managing injuries over the last few weeks, LB Christian Elliss (chest) and S Craig Woodson (shoulder) both playing last week, so one would expect that to continue. The Pats also removed OLB Dre'Mont Jones (shoulder) and OT Morgan Moses (foot) from the injury report – they're good to go.

As for New York, the Jets ruled out three key players for Sunday's game: star RB Breece Hall (quad), WR Adonai Mitchell (finger), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (ankle). Hall is out again this week due to his quad injury, with the Jets explosive lead-back last playing in Week 3. Instead, the Jets will lean on third-year back Braelon Allen. Allen forced eight missed tackles while accumulating 108 yards after contact in rainy conditions vs. the Browns last week, so the power-oriented runner can carry the load.

New England's next steps may include activating players off injured reserve and elevating players from the practice squad. Along with Brown, backup tackle Marcus Bryant (ankle) also returned to practice this week, opening his 21-day window after the team designated him to return on cutdown day. Bryant was pushing to be the top swing tackle during training camp, so his return would boost New England's tackle depth with Campbell's uncertain status.

The Patriots must decide whether to activate Brown and Bryant off injured reserve by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday for them to be eligible to play Sunday. The Pats might also elevate a running back, likely Larison, in case Henderson can't play this week – we'll keep you updated.

The Patriots host the Jets in an AFC East clash at Gillette Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice out Sunday vs. Chargers with hamstring injury - ESPN
authors: Nate Taylor, Matt Bowen, Adam Rank, Brady Henderson, Jeff Legwold, Ryan McFadden, Jordan Raanan, Rich Cimini, Mike Kaye, Eric Woodyard
description:
-- Rashee Rice, the Chiefs' top receiver, is out for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers with a right hamstring injury.
Rice sustained his injury in Week 4 during the Chiefs' comeback win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
In the first quarter of the game, Rice caught a 7-yard reception but stumbled and pulled up while trying to gain yards after the catch, ending the play by going out of bounds.

As part of the Chiefs' 4-0 start, the team's best receivers have been Rice and Thornton.
text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Rashee Rice, the Chiefs' top receiver, is out for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers with a right hamstring injury. He missed each of the team's three practices this week.

Rice sustained his injury in Week 4 during the Chiefs' comeback win over the Las Vegas Raiders. In the first quarter of the game, Rice caught a 7-yard reception but stumbled and pulled up while trying to gain yards after the catch, ending the play by going out of bounds.

Reid suggested it's possible Rice could be available next week when the Chiefs play the Seattle Seahawks on "Sunday Night Football."

"He's out there and wanting to jump in on everything," Reid said of Rice. "He'll be all right. You never know about these [hamstring injuries], but he's a pretty fast healer."

Even before coach Andy Reid shared Friday that Rice would be unavailable, the Chiefs were already without receiver Tyquan Thornton, who was placed on injured reserve earlier this week after suffering a dislocated left ankle. As part of the Chiefs' 4-0 start, the team's best receivers have been Rice and Thornton. The two have combined for 24 catches on 31 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is expected to rely on tight end Travis Kelce and receiver Xavier Worthy to maintain the Chiefs' passing attack. Two young receivers should also see their snaps increase against Chargers: rookie Cyrus Allen and second-year player Jalen Royals.

"They're ready," Mahomes said Wednesday. "They've put in the work. Obviously, we've had the guys in front of them, with Tyquan going out there and playing great, so they've had to put in the work at practice. They're going to step into the role and do their job, so I'm excited for them. We'll put them in [a] position to succeed. I have a lot of trust in those guys."

In training camp, Allen was one of the most impressive players, as he was able to quickly build timing and chemistry with Mahomes.

"They're putting plays in, and I've got a couple packages here and there," Allen said Wednesday of the coaching staff. "I'm just getting ready. I'm more comfortable now. I'm going to be pretty hyped [after my first catch]. I only need one to get me going."

One positive for the Chiefs this week was that left tackle Josh Simmons, the 2025 first-round pick, participated in each of the three practices this week for the first time in almost two months. Simmons has been out with a bulging disc in his lower back. Although Reid said Simmons is also out for Sunday's game, the left tackle was able to begin his process of rebuilding his conditioning to return to the lineup soon to be Mahomes' blind-side protector.

"He's getting better as we go here," Reid said of Simmons. "He didn't work in the team periods [this week], but that was the idea, though, just so he can get a base under him with some fundamentals and techniques and start getting that back. He was excited to be back out there with the guys on the field instead of the meeting room."

title: Eagles sign Joe Milton away from Cowboys after Jalen Hurts injury stunner - NY Post
description:
Philadelphia has signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad, according to multiple reports.
Milton appeared in four games for Dallas in 2025, throwing for 183 yards on 24 attempts with one touchdown and two interceptions.
The team’s statement revealed that Hurts’ blood clot was discovered via ultrasound before their game in London against the Jaguars last Sunday.
The Eagles face Milton’s former Cowboys team in their first of two meeting in a Week 7 “Monday Night Football” matchup on October 26th.
Milton was drafted in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft with the 193rd overall pick by New England.
text:
The Eagles are adding some insurance under center.

Philadelphia has signed quarterback Joe Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad, according to multiple reports.

Milton appeared in four games for Dallas in 2025, throwing for 183 yards on 24 attempts with one touchdown and two interceptions.

The Cowboys traded for Milton before last season after he had an eye-opening season finale for the Patriots in 2024 — completing 22-of-29 passes for 241 yards and a touchdown in a 23-16 win over the Bills.

He again flashed his potential — and tantalizing arm-talent — during this preseason with a three-touchdown game against the Cardinals.

However, the 26-year-old Milton was waived by the Cowboys on Sept. 1 and placed on their practice squad two days later with Sam Howell being named the backup.

Milton will likely join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton on the Eagles’ active roster as the emergency quarterback, meaning he’s unlikely to see much playing time barring any more injuries.

The move comes after news broke Thursday that Hurts would be out indefinitely with a superficial blood clot in his calf, just the latest in a myriad of losses that have hit the Eagles in recent weeks.

The team’s statement revealed that Hurts’ blood clot was discovered via ultrasound before their game in London against the Jaguars last Sunday. A second ultrasound Wednesday revealed the movement of the blood clot, putting Hurts on the shelf indefinitely as the Eagles “determine the appropriate course of treatment.”

McKee will likely be the Eagles’ starter for the time being as they try to get back on track after a 2-3 start in a wide open NFC East.

Sunday’s game against the Panthers will mark McKee’s third career start. His previous two career starts were in end-of-season matchups after the Eagles had secured their spot in the postseason.

The Eagles face Milton’s former Cowboys team in their first of two meeting in a Week 7 “Monday Night Football” matchup on October 26th.

Milton was drafted in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft with the 193rd overall pick by New England.

Milton spent the first three years of his college career at Michigan before transferring to Tennessee.

text:
Even after losing in Week 5, the Atlanta Falcons are clearly trending in the right direction under head coach Kevin Stefanski. The team has gone 2-1 since Michael Penix Jr.'s return, barely losing to the Baltimore Ravens in overtime last weekend.

The Falcons have another tough test coming up against the Chicago Bears in Week 6. Not only is head coach Ben Johnson's team an offensive juggernaut, but the Bears are expecting to get star QB Caleb Williams back this week.

In today's Falcons Wire Recap, Bijan Robinson and Drake London take over as the NFL's best RB-WR duo, Kyle Pitts lands on fantasy sit 'em list, PFF projects Atlanta to take a left tackle in a new mock draft, and we look at the latest injury updates ahead of Sunday's game vs. the Bears.

Falcons release safety Jammie Robinson

The Falcons released defensive back Jammie Robinson on Thursday evening. Robinson, who spent much of the last two seasons on the Falcons' practice squad, was signed to the active roster before Sunday's loss to the Baltimore Ravens. The 25-year-old entered the league as a fifth-round pick with the Carolina Panthers back in 2023.

After playing in 21 games over his first two seasons with the Panthers, Robinson signed with the Falcons in 2025 and appeared in six games. Over his four-year NFL career, Robinson has recorded 23 tackles (16 solo) while contributing primarily on special teams.

Since the Falcons still have a practice squad spot available, we wouldn't be surprised to see Robinson back in Atlanta before Sunday's game against the Bears.

Falcons-Bears injury report: Michael Penix, Caleb Williams updates

Michael Penix Jr. was a full participant at Thursday's practice for the second day in a row. The third-year quarterback is expected to play against Chicago. As for Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, he also appears on track to play on Sunday. The former No. 1 pick was a full participant on Chicago's latest injury report. Falcons defensive end Cameron Thomas was added to Thursday's report (see below).

QB Michael Penix (ribs): FP

LT Jake Matthews (groin): FP

LB Divine Deablo (hamstring): FP

DE Za'Darius Smith (neck): LP

DE Cameron Thomas (groin): LP

CB C.J. Henderson (groin): DNP

RT Jawaan Taylor (rest): DNP

Drake London says Falcons offense nowhere near its ceiling

Michael Penix Jr. re-established his lethal connection with top wide receiver Drake London, who's totaled over 400 receiving yards over the last three games. To hear London tell it, this offense still has a lot of room to grow. Here's what he said about it earlier this week, per Josh Kendall at The Athletic.

“The fun part about this (offense) is that we are nowhere near our ceiling. I truthfully believe that,” London said. “I think we’re going to be … hard to deal with, especially when we clean up some of these little things.”

Falcons have NFL's top RB-WR duo going into Week 6

After scoring just 16 total points in their first two games of the season (8.0 points per game), the Falcons have put up 103 points over the last three weeks (34.3 points per contest) with Penix in the lineup.

Bijan Robinson currently leads the NFL with 580 rushing yards, surpassing Kansas Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker for the top spot going into Week 6. Drake London's production has been off the charts with Penix slinging the rock. The former USC standout's 488 receiving yards rank fourth in the NFL.

Between Robinson and London, the duo has accounted for 1,220 total yards - the highest total of any running back-wide receiver duo in the NFL this season.

Michael Penix Jr. 'good to go' vs. Bears in Week 6

Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. exited Sunday's loss to the Ravens in the fourth quarter with a rib injury and did not return. The third-year quarterback's lengthy injury history has been regurgitated ad nauseam, however, it doesn't sound like Penix is going to miss any time with his rib injury.

"We’re good and I feel good to go this week, so that’s the plan," Penix said following Wednesday's practice. "MRI/scans were all positive... It’s not always comfortable but I made every throw out there today."

Falcons take OT in PFF's new 2027 NFL mock draft

Trevor Goosby from Texas has been the most popular mock pick for Atlanta so far for Round 1, but today we have a new name to digest. A new 2027 NFL mock draft from Pro Football Focus has the Falcons rolling the dice on Jordan Seaton from LSU at No. 14 overall.

"Seaton would give the Falcons a succession plan for Jake Matthews at left tackle, with the veteran currently in his 13th season. LSU's left tackle has earned a 79.1 PFF pass-blocking grade so far in 2026 and produced a 93.5% PFF pass-block win rate on plays where he has been left to block without help." - Gordon McGuinness, PFF

Grady Jarrett excited to face former team

Former Falcons defensive tackle Grady Jarrett, who's undoubtedly one of the best players in franchise history, signed with the Bears in 2025. Jarrett will return to Mercedes-Benz Stadium for the first time since departing in free agency.

The former fifth-round pick out of Clemson spent 10 seasons in Atlanta and served as the face of the defense for the bulk of that span. Jarrett, a Georgia native, recorded 496 tackles (267 solo), 126 QB hits and 36.5 sacks over 152 games with the Falcons.

That would be relevant information, especially as to anyone thinking about wagering hard-earned money through one of the sportsbooks that sponsor the NFL (and in which any NFL team owner can hold up to five-percent of the total equity).

text:
The outside world (including anyone considering placing wagers on the game and/or the specific player’s performance) had no idea that Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts had developed a blood clot in his leg before the team’s Week 5 game in London against the Jaguars. The Eagles, and the league, knew otherwise.

The statement issued by the Eagles on Thursday made it clear that the team was aware of the situation, and that the clot was revealed by an ultrasound examination performed after the team arrived in London. “Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter,” the Eagles said.

Given that the Eagles specifically said the team had “remained in communication with the league office,” we asked the league office whether it had anything to add — specifically as to the question of why Hurts’s status for the game wasn’t changed at any time to “questionable.”

“The team was in contact with the league throughout the process, including the morning of the game,” an NFL spokesperson said via email on Friday morning. “A team would need to make a public announcement immediately if there was any question as to his availability or if he would be impacted in any way. That was not the case here. We would not want a team to list a player as ‘questionable’ on gameday morning when the team knows with 100 percent certainty that he will play in the game. . . . Hurts played 100 percent of the snaps on offense during the game and there was no issue.”

That’s fine, but wasn’t there, at some point, a question as to Hurts’s availability? From the moment it was decided to seek an ultrasound to the moment that the doctors reviewed and analyzed the results, there was an obvious question as to the specific condition that had prompted Hurts to land on the injury report on Friday with a “calf” injury, and whether that condition could keep him from playing.

While Hurts played and took every snap, the league’s current policy (with which the Eagles complied) creates a donut hole of inside information that isn’t shared with the public. Hurts had a blood clot in his leg. That would be relevant information, especially as to anyone thinking about wagering hard-earned money through one of the sportsbooks that sponsor the NFL (and in which any NFL team owner can hold up to five-percent of the total equity).

Whether the NFL revamps its injury-reporting rules on its own or whether the mandate comes from Congress or a regulatory agency, it seems inevitable that more will be required, one of these days. The official injury report from the Eagles didn’t begin to paint the picture as to Hurts’s true condition and status.

Given that, between Saturday and Tuesday, the blood clot moved (making Hurts unavailable for Week 6), it would have been appropriate for the public to know that there was a possibility that, between Saturday and the start of Sunday’s game, the blood clot could move or Hurts’s condition could otherwise deteriorate.

And, yes, it’s possible to have genuine concern for the player’s health while also pointing out the flaws in the current rules that work to the disadvantage of the betting public. Every injury necessarily represents a negative impact on the player’s health. The question becomes whether or not there is sufficient transparency.

Hall has not played since Week 3 due to a quad injury.

Braelon Allen, who ran for 116 yards and a touchdown last week against the Browns, will get be RB1.

After being limited in practice on Wednesday, Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez was a full participant in Thursday's practice, according to the team's injury report.

That upgrade points to a potential return this week, as New England takes on the Jets on Sunday. Gonzalez has missed the last two games while dealing with a shoulder injury.

Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice did not practice on Thursday with multiple injuries, making it likely that Kansas City will be without their top receiver on Sunday. Rice, who left the Chief's Week 4 win over the Raiders early after pulling up awkwardly, is listed as dealing with issues with his hamstring and his knee.

The Chiefs will return to the field on Sunday after a bye last week, but multiple receivers being wiped out with injuries has raised questions. (Things appear worrying enough that Kansas City appears to be weighing other options, like signing Tyreek Hill.)

For the time being, Tanner McKee is tasked with steadying the Eagles' ship. And the waters around Philadelphia are getting pretty rocky these days.

Jalen Hurts being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot is the latest in a deepening injury problem, ruling the quarterback out for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The timing couldn't be worse with the Eagles having lost three straight, the past two in heartbreaking fashion.

McKee was named Hurts' replacement. Andy Dalton had been Hurts' backup to open the season but was cut after an interception against the Bears in Week 3.

McKee has started two career games, both coming in meaningless Week 18 games. Last season, after the Eagles had clinched a playoff spot the week before, McKee completed 21-of-40 passes for 241 yards, one TD and one interception in the 24-17 loss to the Commanders.

The Eagles listed 24 players on this week's injury report, not to mention the five offensive players on injured reserve. The offensive line also took recent hits with the sudden retirement of right tackle Lane Johnson and the trade of left guard Cam Jurgens.

Hurts' injury could be week to week, so it appears McKee could be the starting quarterback during a key stretch of the Eagles' season. After the Panthers, the Eagles face each of their NFC East rivals leading into the Week 10 bye — Monday night against the Cowboys, at the Commanders and home against the division-leading Giants.

Read more here.

The Houston Texans have ruled out running back David Montgomery, safety Jalen Pitre and receiver Tank Dell for Week 6's matchup in London versus the Jacksonville Jaguars. Neither player will make the trip overseas.

Neither Montgomery (groin) nor Pitre (shoulder) have participated in practice this week, after sustaining injuries during Week 5's 26-3 win over the Tennessee Titans.

Dell (knee) was a full participant on Wednesday and Thursday. He missed the entire 2025 season and the first 5 games of 2026 while recovering from a serious injury in which he tore multiple ligaments and damaged his meniscus in 2024.

The status of Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love is up in the air, particularly after the rookie has now missed practice for the second straight day with an ankle injury.

Love, the No. 3 overall pick in this year's draft, has gotten off to a slow start this season.

He's averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, and he's recorded a mere 36 receiving yards. Love entered the league with impeccable prospects, both as a ball carrier and as a receiver out of the backfield.

The Cardinals will face the Los Angeles Rams on the road this week.

Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was a full participant in Thursday's practice and expects to play against the Green Bay Packers in Week 6.

Porter sat out Week 5's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, his second game with the Cowboys after being traded from the Pittsburgh Steelers, after becoming ill on gameday.

"I really just couldn't hold anything down," Porter said on the Cowboys' official website. "You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn't hold in deep down."

text:
Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss Sunday's game against the Panthers because of a superficial blood clot in his calf, the team announced Thursday.

In a statement, the Eagles said that Hurts visited the training room after a practice on Oct. 8 for treatment on his calf, informing the staff that he had been cleated during the game against the Rams on Oct. 4. He practiced in full that week.

The staff performed an ultrasound on Hurts when he arrived in London on Saturday "out of an abundance of caution," and it revealed a superficial blood clot that he could play through.

"Our medical staff and doctors in London reviewed the results and concluded that activity and mobility were important and that Jalen could safely play," the statement said. "Doctors recommended a follow-up ultrasound within 72 hours of the game and the return flight to Philadelphia."

According to the Cleveland Clinic, "superficial thrombophlebitis, or superficial vein thrombosis, is a blood clot that occurs in veins under the skin (superficial veins)."

On Sunday, Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the 19-17 loss to the Jaguars. He rushed for two yards, his lowest output of the season.

MORE BY JIMMY HASCUP

Giants' Malik Nabers suffers injury scare against Rams ... but he returnsSep. 21, 2026, 9:24 p.m.

Mets trade Clay Holmes in deal to acquire new No. 1 prospectAug. 3, 2026, 6:13 p.m.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday, received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report," the Eagles said. "On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

Wrote Dr. Brian Sutterer on X, "Oo boy - if this has progressed to a deep vein clot instead of lower risk superficial (Hurts) could be looking at the end of his season. Treatment for that would be blood thinners often for multiple months and the standard is no contact sports while on blood thinners."

Wrote Dr. Tom Christ on X: "Report that he has a superficial blood clot in his lower leg, not a deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Still, this is medically complicated and needs cautious care. DVTs are far worse and would have him out for months, SuVT can still cost substantial time if he needs to go on anticoagulants. Right now with the limited intel released there's no way to project the rest of his season and time missed. We'll await more reports."

text:
SANTA CLARA — Christian Kirk was a spectator for the first five games of the regular season.

Now, he is getting closer to making a difference for the 49ers.

Kirk has been sidelined for nearly three months with a calf injury. The 49ers opened his practice window on Thursday, and now it is up to him to earn his spot off injured reserve and onto the 53-man roster.

“I believe I have a lot of really good football left,” Kirk said on Thursday. “In no way, shape or form, I thought about anything other than that. It's just all about working to get my body back to feeling great, to be able to go out and play.”

Kirk, 29, is a nine-year NFL veteran. He has 432 receptions for 5,415 yards and 30 touchdowns in his career. Last year, he caught 28 passes for 239 yards and a touchdown in 13 games with the Houston Texans.

He was ultra-productive in the postseason, catching 10 passes for 164 yards and two touchdowns in two playoff games for Houston.

There is an opportunity for Kirk to make an impact with the 49ers. Deebo Samuel is expected to be out until after the bye week with a hamstring injury. Demarcus Robinson is nearing a return from a high-ankle sprain. Rookie De’Zhaun Stribling could be out until late-November after undergoing ankle surgery.

San Francisco 49ers

Find the latest San Francisco 49ers news, highlights, analysis and more with NBC Sports Bay Area and California.

In addition, the team’s top wide receiver, Mike Evans, sat out practice with ribs and Achilles soreness. Evans is expected to be available to play Monday night against the Washington Commanders at Levi’s Stadium.

Kirk went through limited practice on Thursday, as he hopes to get up to speed quickly. Other than Evans, the other receivers on the 49ers’ 53-man roster are Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing.

The 49ers are one of just three unbeaten teams in the NFL at 5-0 and all alone atop the NFC West standings.

Kirk said he is looking forward to making a contribution toward victories as the season progresses.

“It's like riding a bike,” He said. “I’ve been doing it for a while. And so for me, it's just getting back out there, getting integrated with the guys.

“Obviously, it's been hard not being out there. But it’s been really cool to watch day-in and day-out, how this team comes to work every single day, for it to be able to carry over on Sundays.”

Through his previous eight NFL seasons, Kirk played nine games against the 49ers — mostly during his first four NFL seasons with the Arizona Cardinals.

So he thought he knew a lot about the organization. Still, it has been enlightening seeing how the team operates behind the scenes.

“But now being in the building, and just seeing the approach, seeing the mentality, the mindset day-in and day-out, I think it's been the coolest thing for me to see," Kirk said. "Just the leadership and how those guys take over.

“I’m just ready to be a part of it on the field.”

title: CTE study on NFL players raises questions about California's youth concussion protocol

If a concussion is confirmed, the student must complete a gradual return-to-play protocol lasting at least seven days.
The California Interscholastic Federation, which established the state’s student athlete concussion protocol, said it’s important for everyone involved to make sure the return-to-play process is followed.

text:
There is renewed concern about whether enough is being done to prevent the youth sports concussions following a major study that found at least a quarter of NFL players are expected to develop a degenerative brain disease.

“What’s happening when these individuals are younger? How many little hits are they getting that leads to them having CTE? And what can we do at that younger age group to prevent these athletes from getting that?” asked Dr. Nirav Pandya, a pediatric orthopedic surgeon with UCSF Benioff who specializes in sports medicine for young athletes.

Concussions in general affect around two million teenagers and children in the U.S. every year, according to the National Center for Health Statistics.

Boys tackle football has the highest rate of concussions, according to the CDC, and girls soccer is number two. Girls in general have a higher change of sports-related concussions than boys, the agency said, in part because girls may report more and health care professionals like athletic trainers are less likely to be at girls’ practices and games to identify injuries.

California’s student athlete concussion protocol

In California, school coaches are required to take an online training course on concussions. If they suspect a concussion, they must remove the student athlete from the game or practice for at least that day until cleared by a licensed health care provider. If a concussion is confirmed, the student must complete a gradual return-to-play protocol lasting at least seven days.

“I think the tough thing with all of this is that you are basing it on a kid reporting symptoms and someone identifying them,” said Dr. Pandya who said he recently had a patient whose concussions went undiagnosed for over a year.

“He had horrible headaches, had problems learning for over a year and had multiple concussions and hadn't gotten treatment,” Dr. Pandya said. “A concussion, there’s no MRI; no blood test for it.”

Ben Nguyen’s concussion story

The Investigative Unit

Have a tip for The Investigative Unit? Call 1-888-996-TIPS.

Earlier this year, Ben Nguyen, a senior at Archbishop Mitty High School in San Jose, California, says he suffered a serious concussion during a wrestling match.

“I felt incredibly nauseous,” he recalled.

Nguyen shared cell phone video of the moment he got concussed. It showed his opponent go in for a takedown when Nguyen responds by trying to flip the other student over his own body.

“His should and neck were kind of in my chin area,” he said. “The impact kind of went straight to my head.”

The impact wasn’t obvious, but the symptoms afterward were.

“I couldn’t think as fast anymore…I was like throwing up in the bus ride. I was throwing up right after my match as well,” Nguyen said.

Nguyen said he felt a little nervous about telling his coach and athletic trainer, who’s a sports health care professional on the team.

“The impact looked so subtle. I was kind of scared of them being like, ‘Oh, there’s nothing, you can go back,’” Nguyen said. He said that didn’t happen and his school took his injury seriously. However, he admits, it’s easy for students to get around the concussion protocols if they want.

“I have a friend in football who had all the hallmark symptoms of concussions, he just lied on the survey to get back into practice,” he said.

NBC Bay Area reached out to Archbishop Mitty High School. The school declined to participate in this story. The California Interscholastic Federation, which established the state’s student athlete concussion protocol, said it’s important for everyone involved to make sure the return-to-play process is followed.

The solutions, the science, and the debate

“If we can empower kids to understand that it's okay to speak up. Number two, the system, athletic trainers, physical therapists, anyone who's looking over these kids.Then, I think there are more drastic things that we talk about like, how can we decrease the number of chances or times that someone can get hit? Maybe that means delaying when kids start playing tackle football,” Dr. Pandya said.

It’s some of those drastic suggestions that continue to get pushback.

“My big concern is when we hear results about people who play the most elite level, that there's a reaction of looking at, well, what do we do at the youth level? And these are very different games,” said David Camarillo who is Associate Professor of Bioengineering, (by courtesy) Mechanical Engineering and Neurosurgery at Stanford University.

Camarillo has been studying concussions for the past 15 years testing thousands of helmets in his lab, CamLab, in Stanford.

The results he’s talking about come from a recent study published in the British Medical Journal showing at least a quarter of NFL players will likely develop a neurodegenerative disease like CTE. The NFL said it’s aware of the study, and it’s ensuring its community has access to expanding resources. Camarillo believes the science points to urgent action needed at the professional level.

“Does it mean kids shouldn't play sports? I don't think we have enough information to say yes to that,” Camarillo said.

When asked what’s the harm in taking preventative action in case certain youth sports are connected to developing CTE later in life, Camarillo said he believes taking action at an individual level is perfectly fair.

“I think it's a very different thing to make a law, to make public policy that affects everybody, that takes away a right to choose. That ought to have scientific evidence behind it,” he added.

Why isn’t there evidence? The British Medical Journal study relied on hundreds of NFL players donating their brains to science after they die. We don’t have that kind of data on our young athletes today.

The Investigative Unit spoke to numerous doctors, researchers, and students about this issue over the past several weeks. All said the best solution right now is education and schools fostering a culture where students feel encouraged to report concussion symptoms.

“If it wasn't for like my prior knowledge or like my friends or like me witnessing it first-hand, I probably would have lied to get back into wrestling,” Nguyen said.

text:
New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick told reporters on Thursday that he was fined by the NFL for his helmet-to-helmet hit on Cleveland Browns receiver KC Concepcion during Week 5's 17-12 win. However, the nine-year veteran intends to appeal the fine.

The play in question occurred during the first quarter when Concepcion went up for a deep throw from Deshaun Watson and was hit hard by Fitzpatrick. Two flags were quickly thrown by officials and the Jets safety was flagged for a 15-yard penalty.

Concepcion was down on the turf for several minutes before trainers helped him to his feet. He was immediately taken to the locker room and soon ruled out for the remainder of the game.

Closer angles on the hit showed that Concepcion may have been knocked out, with his eyes rolling back as he laid on the field. In addition to the collision with Fitzpatrick, the rookie receiver's head hit the MetLife Stadium turf, causing his neck to bend forward.

Fitzpatrick did not say how much he was fined. A first offense for "impermissible use of the helmet/launching" carries a $23,882 fine, while a second offense draws a $47,762 deduction, according to the NFL website.

"It was a football play, in my opinion," Fitzpatrick said. "Obviously, you don't like to see anybody get hurt. I'm happy to see he's back and practicing this week."

Fitzpatrick then referred to Browns coach Todd Monken calling the hit "a bang-bang play" and saying he didn't think the safety was a dirty player.

While Concepcion did return to practice, as Fitzpatrick mentioned, he was a limited participant on Wednesday and Thursday as he continues to be in the NFL's concussion protocol.

"I understand why I got the penalty," Fitzpatrick added, via the New York Daily News. "It wasn't for targeting or hitting him in the head. It was for hitting a defenseless player. In my opinion, when a receiver has the ball, you have every right to hit him as long as you are not hitting him in the head."

Fitzpatrick may have also drawn an additional fine for committing a facemask penalty earlier in the game on Concepcion in which the receiver's helmet was ripped off. If so, he didn't indicate he incurred another fine.

Browns fans already held a grudge against Fitzpatrick for a hit on running back Nick Chubb that caused a serious, season-ending knee injury in 2023. The safety was with the Pittsburgh Steelers at the time.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles revealed that quarterback Jalen Hurts has been dealing with a calf injury, which involves a blood clot.

Originally, per the team, Hurts informed the Eagles' training staff that he was cleated in the calf during the team's Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams, with an ultrasound later showing a superficial blood clot, but the quarterback was cleared to play in their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

"Jalen played without limitation in the game Sunday [Week 5 against the Jaguars], received treatment on Monday and Tuesday, and practiced in full on Wednesday, as reflected in the practice report. Throughout our time in London and this week, we have remained in communication with the league office regarding the matter. On Wednesday night, a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot," the Eagles said in a statement on Thursday afternoon.

"Jalen will be out for Sunday's game vs. the [Carolina] Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment. His health and safety are our highest priority."

With Hurts out, Philadelphia's quarterback room includes the third-year Tanner McKee, who has made two NFL starts, and rookie Cole Payton.

Through five games, Hurts, a three-time Pro Bowler, has totaled 933 passing yards, eight passing touchdowns, three interceptions and an 84.7 passer rating, while completing 57.8% of his passes.

Hurts' passer rating and completion percentage are each career lows since becoming the Eagles' full-time quarterback in 2021. He has also rushed for 107 yards and one touchdown.

After winning their first two games of the season against the Washington Commanders and Tennessee Titans, the Eagles have lost three consecutive games to the Chicago Bears, Rams and Jaguars. Philadelphia's loss to Jacksonville came via a 57-yard field goal as time expired from Jaguars kicker Cam Little.
